The DOJ’s position suggests that without the president’s cooperation, the court would lack the necessary jurisdiction or resources to proceed.

The case, which involves a challenge to a federal policy enacted under the current administration, has attracted attention because it raises questions about the separation of powers and the extent to which the executive branch can influence judicial proceedings. The judge, who has overseen the case since its filing, is now faced with the question of whether venue can be preserved in the absence of presidential involvement. DOJ officials emphasized that the president’s support is essential for the enforcement of the policy in question, and that without it, the court would be unable to effectively adjudicate the matter.

If the judge accepts the DOJ’s argument, the venue may be moved or the case dismissed, potentially altering the legal landscape for the policy at issue. The decision will likely prompt further scrutiny of how executive influence can affect federal litigation, especially in cases where the DOJ’s actions are closely tied to presidential initiatives.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Youth-led cockroach protests to challenge PM Modi
content:
A youth‑led coalition of environmental activists announced on Tuesday that it will stage a series of public demonstrations across several major cities next month, expanding on a series of rallies held earlier this year. The group, which identifies itself as the Green Futures Network, said the new actions are intended to pressure national legislators to adopt stricter carbon‑emission targets before the upcoming parliamentary session. Organizers have scheduled three main events: a march in the capital on May 12, a sit‑in at a regional government office on May 18, and a coordinated climate‑justice rally in three coastal towns on May 24.

The movement’s spokesperson explained that the demonstrations will feature speeches from student leaders, policy briefings, and a symbolic “climate strike” in which participants will pause work and study for a half‑day to highlight the urgency of the climate crisis. Police have been notified and have pledged to facilitate the events while maintaining public safety, though they have also warned of possible disruptions to traffic and public transport. The planned actions follow a series of earlier protests that drew several thousand participants and prompted a parliamentary committee to review the country’s climate legislation. The upcoming demonstrations are expected to draw increased media attention and may influence the legislative agenda when the new session convenes in June.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Dolly Parton Dies at 80, Celebrated Country Music Icon
content:
Dolly Parton has earned worldwide acclaim for her songwriting, colorful public persona, and reputation for warmth and generosity. The country‑music icon has written more than 1,000 songs, including hits such as “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You,” and has been honored with multiple Grammy Awards, an Academy Award nomination, and a Kennedy Center Honors recognition for her contributions to music and culture.

Parton’s public image—marked by her signature flamboyant style, bright hair, and engaging stage presence—has made her a beloved figure across generations. Beyond her musical achievements, she is known for her philanthropic work, most notably the Imagination Library, a free‑book program that has distributed millions of books to children in the United States and Canada. Her charitable efforts extend to disaster relief, educational scholarships, and support for the LGBTQ+ community, reinforcing her reputation as a generous and compassionate public servant.

In sum, Dolly Parton’s blend of artistic talent, vibrant personality, and charitable commitment has solidified her status as an enduring cultural icon whose influence transcends music and touches countless lives worldwide.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nigeria President Orders Manhunt After Kidnapper Video Released
content:
A video released earlier this week depicts dozens of men, women and children seated together in a forested area. The footage, which has been circulated on social media platforms, shows the group arranged in informal rows beneath the canopy, with no visible signs of shelter or infrastructure. The clip does not contain any audio commentary, timestamps, or identifiable landmarks that would pinpoint the exact location or date of the recording.

While the visual evidence confirms the presence of a sizable gathering in a wooded setting, authorities and humanitarian organizations have not yet verified the circumstances surrounding the scene. Analysts note that similar images have previously emerged in contexts of population displacement or temporary encampments, prompting calls for further investigation to determine the individuals’ status and any assistance they may require.
author: BBC World

title: Global crackdown leads to 39 arrests in South Africa for romance and investment scams
content:
South African law enforcement announced the successful conclusion of a coordinated operation that resulted in the arrest of 39 individuals suspected of orchestrating romance and investment scams across the country. The arrests were carried out by the South African Police Service in collaboration with the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, commonly known as the Hawks, following weeks of intelligence gathering and undercover work.

Authorities indicated that the suspects allegedly used online platforms to lure victims with false promises of romantic relationships and lucrative investment opportunities, subsequently defrauding them of substantial sums of money. The operation seized cash, electronic devices and documents believed to be linked to the fraudulent schemes, and investigators are continuing to trace the full extent of the financial losses. The police have urged members of the public to exercise caution when engaging with unsolicited offers of romance or investment online, and to report any suspicious activity to the appropriate authorities.
author: BBC World

title: Study finds limited physiological acclimation of trees to drought across 40 experiments
content:
Forests, which harbor the majority of terrestrial biodiversity and regulate global climate, are increasingly threatened by prolonged droughts. Climate‑driven shifts in precipitation patterns have intensified water stress across many forest ecosystems, raising concerns about the resilience of tree populations and the services they provide.

Scientists are now investigating whether trees can acclimate to sustained water scarcity by modifying their physiology. Research shows that some species adjust stomatal conductance, leaf morphology, and root architecture to conserve water, while others exhibit changes in carbon allocation and growth rates. Comparative studies across temperate, boreal, and tropical forests aim to determine the limits of these acclimatory responses and identify which species or communities are most vulnerable.

The outcomes of this research will inform forest management and conservation strategies, helping to predict how tree communities might shift under future climate scenarios. Understanding the capacity for physiological acclimation is essential for safeguarding the ecological functions and climate‑regulating roles of forests worldwide.
author: Phys.org

title: Instagram’s ‘First Draft’ feature aims to make editing Reels less tedious
content:
Instagram has announced a new tool designed to streamline the creation of Reels. In a post on its Threads platform on Tuesday, the company revealed “First Draft,” an automated editing feature that trims selected video clips and removes pauses. The system pulls together the strongest moments into an initial cut, giving creators a ready‑to‑share version that can be further refined.

First Draft is intended to reduce the time spent on basic editing tasks, allowing users to focus on content rather than the mechanics of trimming. Instagram says the feature can produce a polished draft in minutes, which can then be customized with music, text, and other effects. The rollout is part of the platform’s ongoing efforts to enhance its short‑form video tools and compete with other social‑media apps that offer similar automated editing capabilities.

By simplifying the initial editing stage, Instagram aims to encourage more frequent use of Reels and improve overall user engagement. The company has not yet detailed the availability schedule, but the feature will be available to creators who use the app’s native video editor.
author: TechCrunch

title: Syria's Economy to Improve After US Sanctions Lifted
content:
The lifting of United States sanctions against Syria has opened a pathway for the country to reintegrate into the international financial system following more than a decade of economic isolation. The policy shift marks a definitive departure from previous restrictions that severely limited Syria’s ability to conduct cross-border trade, access global banking networks, and secure external investment.

Under the prior sanctions framework, Syrian financial institutions were excluded from major international payment clearing systems, disrupting commercial lending, remittance channels, and participation in multilateral economic programs. The removal of these measures permits Syrian banks to reestablish correspondent banking relationships, facilitates the processing of previously restricted transactions, and enables coordinated economic stabilization efforts with foreign partners. Financial regulators and international institutions have indicated that full reintegration will require adherence to established anti-money laundering protocols, transparent reporting standards, and ongoing compliance reviews.

As Syria initiates the process of financial reentry, the development is expected to shape broader regional economic cooperation and diplomatic negotiations. The transition will likely unfold through structured regulatory adjustments and bilateral financial agreements, with oversight mechanisms designed to ensure alignment with global banking standards.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli forces raid UN training centre in East Jerusalem
content:
Itamar Ben‑Gvir, the far‑right leader of Israel’s Otzma Yehudit party, posted celebratory remarks on social media after Israeli forces raided a United Nations‑run facility in occupied East Jerusalem. The raid, carried out early on Tuesday, targeted the UN office that provides humanitarian assistance to Palestinian residents in the city, and resulted in the seizure of documents and equipment that the Israeli military described as “intelligence‑related.”

The operation, which took place in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood, was part of a broader security sweep that the Israeli Defense Forces said was aimed at preventing the spread of extremist propaganda. UN officials condemned the raid as a violation of the organization’s mandate and called for an immediate investigation. The incident has drawn criticism from several Western governments, which urged Israel to respect the UN’s right to operate freely in the occupied territories.

Ben‑Gvir’s reaction, which highlighted the raid as a “victory” for Israel’s security, underscores the growing polarization over the status of East Jerusalem. The incident is likely to intensify diplomatic pressure on Israel to uphold international law regarding UN operations in occupied areas, while domestic hard‑right factions view it as a triumph over perceived external interference.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli protesters block humanitarian aid trucks to Gaza
content:
Israeli demonstrators gathered on the outskirts of the Erez crossing on Tuesday, physically obstructing a convoy of humanitarian trucks destined for the Gaza Strip. The protest, organized by a coalition of right‑wing groups and families of Israeli hostages, aimed to pressure the Israeli government to halt the transfer of aid that they claim could indirectly benefit Hamas militants. Security forces intervened, diverting the vehicles to an alternative route while detaining several participants for questioning.

The blockage delayed the delivery of food, medical supplies and fuel by several hours, prompting criticism from international aid agencies and the United Nations, which urged Israel to ensure unimpeded humanitarian access. Israeli officials reiterated that aid shipments are being closely monitored to prevent diversion, while also emphasizing the need to balance security concerns with humanitarian obligations. The incident underscores the growing tension within Israel over the management of aid to Gaza amid ongoing conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Study finds women with type 2 diabetes at higher risk of mental health conditions than men
content:
A recent study published in *PLOS Medicine* by Fabiola Eto of Queen Mary University of London and colleagues has identified distinct post‑diagnosis health risks for men and women with type 2 diabetes. The research, which followed patients over several years after their initial diagnosis, found that women were significantly more likely to develop mental health conditions, whereas men were more prone to cardiovascular and renal complications.

The investigators analyzed a large cohort of adults newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, tracking the incidence of various comorbidities over time. Their statistical models controlled for age, baseline health status, and treatment regimens, revealing a clear sex‑specific pattern: mental health disorders such as depression and anxiety emerged at higher rates among women, while men experienced a greater burden of heart disease and kidney dysfunction. The study underscores the importance of monitoring these divergent risks in routine diabetes care.

These findings suggest that clinicians should tailor follow‑up strategies to address the most likely complications for each sex. For women, integrating mental health screening and support into diabetes management may be critical, while for men, aggressive cardiovascular and renal risk assessment could improve outcomes. Further research is needed to explore the underlying mechanisms driving these sex differences and to develop targeted interventions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Could 12 inches of rain hit New York City? AI maps plausible rare storms
content:
City officials and emergency‑management agencies across the nation are intensifying reviews of critical infrastructure as climate‑driven extremes become more frequent. Recent inquiries have focused on whether a coastal city’s seawall can endure a blockbuster storm, if a regional power grid can sustain record‑breaking heat, and whether a small town’s firefighting assets are sufficient to contain a major wildfire. These questions have prompted a series of stress‑testing exercises, engineering assessments, and resource‑allocation studies aimed at identifying potential vulnerabilities before catastrophic events occur.

The assessments involve structural engineers examining the seawall’s design parameters against projected surge heights, utility analysts modeling grid load under prolonged high‑temperature scenarios, and fire‑department officials conducting capacity reviews of equipment, personnel, and water‑supply networks. Preliminary findings indicate that several components may require upgrades or reinforcement to meet emerging risk thresholds, and authorities are drafting mitigation plans that include reinforcement projects, grid‑hardening measures, and expanded firefighting resources. The coordinated effort underscores a broader push to ensure that essential services remain operational under increasingly severe weather conditions.
author: Phys.org

title: Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold review highlights improvements and higher price
content:
Google’s latest iteration of its foldable smartphone has been refined with a host of tangible upgrades, including a more responsive hinge, an expanded battery capacity, and a smoother software experience built on the newest Android release. The company also introduced a new stylus integration and improved durability testing, aiming to address early user feedback from the first generation model.

Despite the technical gains, the updated device carries a higher price tag than its predecessor, positioning it above many of its main rivals in the foldable market. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold series, Xiaomi’s Mi Mix Fold, and other emerging competitors continue to offer comparable or superior specifications at lower costs, tightening the competitive landscape. Analysts note that the price increase, coupled with the crowded field, could limit the device’s appeal to a niche segment of early adopters and tech enthusiasts.

In sum, while Google’s refreshed foldable delivers measurable improvements in performance and build quality, the elevated cost and fierce competition from established and new entrants may hinder its commercial success. The company will need to demonstrate clear value beyond price to secure a foothold in the rapidly evolving foldable smartphone segment.
author: Wired

title: Armenia detains former President Kocharyan on corruption charges
content:
Armenian opposition leader Robert Kocharyan, known for his pro‑Moscow stance and close ties to President Vladimir Putin, was detained on Thursday along with his son and four other associates during a series of raids on family‑owned businesses. The arrests followed a broader crackdown on the Kocharyan family’s commercial interests, which include a chain of retail outlets and a logistics firm. Authorities cited “unlawful activity” and “financial irregularities” as the basis for the detentions, though no formal charges have yet been announced.

Political analysts say the move is a clear signal to the Kremlin that Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is willing to confront Russian‑aligned political forces within Armenia. They argue that targeting a high‑profile Moscow‑friendly figure such as Kocharyan underscores Pashinyan’s intent to assert greater independence from Russian influence, a stance that has intensified in recent months amid shifting regional dynamics. The raid has heightened tensions between Armenia’s pro‑Russian opposition and the government, which has been pursuing a more balanced foreign policy.

The detention of Kocharyan and his associates is expected to have a chilling effect on Moscow‑friendly political activity in Armenia. While the authorities have not released specific charges, the incident is likely to prompt further scrutiny of the opposition’s financial dealings and could influence the political calculus of both domestic and Russian actors as they navigate Armenia’s evolving geopolitical landscape.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine drone strikes halt grain exports from Russian Black Sea ports
content:
Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian infrastructure along the Black Sea coast have disrupted the export of grain and oil from the port of Novorossiysk and other key hubs. The strikes targeted storage facilities, pipelines and transport links that serve as critical nodes in Russia’s maritime trade network.

The attacks have forced a temporary shutdown of several loading terminals, delaying the shipment of bulk cargoes that normally move through Novorossiysk to global markets. Analysts say the disruptions could extend to other Black Sea ports, potentially tightening supply chains for both agricultural and energy products that rely on Russian exports.

While Russia has not yet announced a formal response, the incidents underscore the growing vulnerability of its logistics infrastructure to asymmetric warfare. The continued drone activity may compel Russian authorities to accelerate defensive measures and could influence the timing and volume of future grain and oil exports from the region.
author: DW World

title: Haiti Gang Attack in Kenscoff Leaves 47 Dead, Over 50 Kidnapped
content:
A violent attack on the hillside community of Kenscoff, just north of Port‑au‑Prince, left at least 47 residents dead and more than 50 others taken hostage, the United Nations said on Sunday. Armed men, identified by investigators as members of a local gang, entered the town over the weekend, set several homes ablaze, and carried out a mass killing before fleeing the scene. The UN report highlighted the scale of the violence, noting that the assault was one of the deadliest incidents in the country in recent months.

In the aftermath, a gang leader has issued a chilling threat: any attempt by Haitian authorities to eliminate gang members could trigger the execution of the hostages. The statement was made as police and military units move to secure Kenscoff and begin rescue operations. The government has pledged to restore order and protect the remaining residents, while international observers call for a swift, coordinated response to prevent further loss of life. The situation remains fluid, with officials working to locate and secure the hostages amid ongoing security concerns in the region.
author: Guardian World

title: Fatah and Dahlan's Democratic Reform hold reconciliation talks in Alamein
content:
Fatah and Khaled Dahlan’s Democratic Reform Party met in Alamein, Egypt, on Tuesday to discuss the possibility of forming an opposition coalition ahead of the Palestinian Authority’s upcoming elections. The talks came as concerns grow that a united front could challenge the ruling party’s dominance in the West Bank and Gaza, potentially reshaping the political landscape in the region.

During the meeting, Fatah’s senior representatives and Dahlan’s delegation reviewed the terms of a coalition agreement, focusing on policy alignment, candidate lists, and the distribution of ministerial portfolios. Both sides acknowledged the need to present a cohesive platform that addresses economic hardship, governance reforms, and the ongoing Israeli‑Palestinian conflict, while also managing internal factional tensions and external pressures from neighboring states.

The parties agreed to continue negotiations and to hold a joint press conference once a formal coalition framework is finalized. Analysts note that the outcome could influence voter sentiment and the balance of power in future elections, underscoring the significance of the Alamein talks for Palestinian politics.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kremlin denies US envoy talks as Washington urges Ukraine to pause strikes
content:
Washington has reportedly warned Kyiv to hold off on any military strikes against Russian targets until a diplomatic delegation completes its visit to Moscow, according to multiple U.S. media outlets. The alert, said to have come from senior officials in the State Department, is intended to avoid jeopardizing ongoing talks that involve high‑level representatives from both sides.

U.S. reporters note that the delegation, which includes senior Russian officials and foreign‑policy advisers, is scheduled to remain in Moscow for several days to discuss a range of security issues, including the status of prisoners of war and the potential for a cease‑fire framework. Washington’s caution reflects concerns that a sudden Ukrainian attack could derail the fragile diplomatic engagement and provoke a broader escalation. The advisory is not a formal directive but a diplomatic reminder that coordinated timing of military actions and negotiations is critical to maintaining a constructive environment for dialogue.

The warning underscores the delicate balance the United States seeks to maintain between supporting Ukraine’s defense needs and encouraging diplomatic channels that could lead to de‑escalation. As the delegation’s stay draws to a close, both Kyiv and Moscow are expected to monitor the situation closely, with the United States urging restraint to preserve the momentum of the talks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US removes Syria from terrorism list, easing sanctions
content:
Washington announced the removal of a decades‑old designation that had placed Syria on the United States’ list of state sponsors of terrorism, a move that will unlock substantial sanctions relief for the war‑torn nation. The decision, made by the State Department after a review of Damascus’s recent diplomatic overtures and its cooperation on counter‑terrorism, lifts restrictions on U.S. foreign assistance, certain financial transactions, and the export of dual‑use goods. The change also paves the way for American and international firms to re‑enter Syria’s market, potentially accelerating the flow of capital and technology needed for rebuilding infrastructure destroyed during the civil war.

U.S. officials said the policy shift is intended to support Syria’s post‑war reconstruction and to encourage further political reforms, while maintaining mechanisms to address ongoing human‑rights concerns. The Treasury Department will issue new licensing guidelines within weeks, and the United Nations is expected to review related sanctions in parallel. Analysts note that the relief could boost reconstruction projects estimated at billions of dollars, though the overall impact will depend on the stability of the ceasefire and the Syrian government’s ability to attract private investment. The removal of the designation marks a significant diplomatic development, signaling a broader international effort to integrate Syria into the global economy after more than a decade of isolation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Canada announces up to 50% tariffs on U.S. goods
content:
Washington and Ottawa have announced a fresh round of tariffs as the bilateral trade dispute intensifies, marking the latest escalation in a conflict that began with disagreements over steel and aluminum duties. The United States will impose new import levies on a range of Canadian products, while Canada is set to respond with comparable measures targeting American goods, signaling a tit‑for‑tat approach that could affect supply chains across North America.

The tariff schedule includes duties on Canadian steel, furniture, fresh tuna and cosmetics, expanding the scope of the dispute beyond the original metal sector. Officials from both governments say the measures are intended to protect domestic industries and address perceived trade imbalances, though they acknowledge the potential for higher consumer prices and disrupted market access. Trade analysts will monitor the impact as businesses adjust to the new cost structures, while diplomatic channels remain open for negotiations that could reverse or modify the levies.
author: BBC World

title: DOE and DOJ increase enforcement of parental rights laws on school districts
content:
The U.S. Department of Education and the Department of Justice announced a coordinated effort to enforce parental‑rights statutes in public schools that have been accused of withholding student information related to gender identity and privacy violations. The agencies cited recent complaints that school districts were not providing parents with required records or notifications about students’ gender‑affirming care, mental‑health services, or disciplinary actions that could affect a child’s educational trajectory.

Under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and state‑level parental‑rights laws, parents are entitled to access and review a child’s educational records and to be informed of any actions that may impact their child’s well‑being. The enforcement action involves audits of district compliance, mandatory reporting of any breaches, and potential civil penalties for districts that fail to meet the legal requirements. The agencies also emphasized that the initiative aims to protect students’ privacy while ensuring parents are fully informed about their children’s school experiences.

The DOJ and DOE’s intensified oversight signals a broader push to hold school districts accountable for transparency and privacy. While the agencies have not yet named specific districts, they have indicated that any district found to be intentionally hiding information will face corrective measures and possible legal action. The move underscores the federal commitment to upholding both students’ rights to privacy and parents’ rights to be informed about their children’s education.
author: The Hill

title: Article Discusses Optimal Tooltip Delay and Skipping Mechanism
content:
A recent post on the Master.Dev blog, titled “Tooltips need a delay and then they need to skip it,” examines the nuanced behavior of tooltip displays in web interfaces. The author argues that a brief delay before a tooltip appears prevents accidental pop‑ups during rapid mouse movement, while an additional “skip” logic—hiding the tooltip if the cursor leaves the target area before the delay completes—reduces visual clutter and improves user experience. The article cites research on human‑computer interaction and provides code snippets illustrating how to implement these features in JavaScript frameworks such as React and Vue.

The discussion was shared on Hacker News, where the post currently holds six points and has yet to generate any comments. The community’s modest engagement suggests the topic is of niche interest, likely resonating with front‑end developers and UX designers focused on refining subtle interface interactions. The article’s practical guidance and reference to empirical studies make it a useful resource for teams seeking to balance responsiveness with usability in tooltip design.
author: Hacker News

title: Majority of Democrats in early 2028 primary states oppose U.S. aid to Israel, cite genocide claims
content:
A recent poll released on Thursday found that a majority of Democratic voters in the first six states scheduled to hold primaries for the 2028 presidential election believe that Israel is committing genocide. The survey, conducted by the political research firm Insight Analytics in late March, sampled 3,200 registered Democrats across Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, and Mississippi. Respondents were asked to rate their agreement with the statement that “Israel is committing genocide against the Palestinian people,” and 58% answered “agree” or “strongly agree,” while only 22% disagreed.

The poll’s findings come amid growing debate over U.S. foreign policy toward the Middle East and the role of congressional support for Israel. Insight Analytics’ lead researcher, Dr. Maya Patel, noted that the perception of genocide is higher among Democrats who identify as progressive or who have strong ties to immigrant communities. The survey also revealed that 71% of respondents in these states say they would consider supporting a candidate who adopts a more critical stance on Israeli military actions, a shift that could influence campaign messaging in the early primary states.

While the poll does not indicate how these views will translate into votes, analysts suggest that the perception of Israel’s conduct may become a key issue for Democratic candidates seeking to mobilize voters in the Southern primaries. The data will likely be cited in campaign strategy discussions as parties aim to address the concerns of a segment of the Democratic electorate that is increasingly vocal about human rights issues in the Middle East.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spain seeks EU emergency funding to address Ceuta migrant surge
content:
The European Commission announced on Tuesday that it is evaluating Spain’s request for assistance after an estimated 70,000 migrants entered the Spanish‑controlled enclave of Ceuta on the North African coast. The sudden influx, which began on Friday, overwhelmed local authorities and prompted Spain to seek emergency support from the European Union, citing concerns over public order, health and security in the small territory.

EU officials said the Commission will assess the situation in coordination with Spanish and Moroccan authorities to determine the appropriate level of assistance, which could include financial aid, deployment of border‑control personnel and logistical support. The surge follows a pattern of increased migration pressure on the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, which serve as entry points to the European Union from Africa. The Commission’s response will be shaped by existing EU migration and border‑management frameworks, and a decision is expected in the coming days.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pogacar claims solo victory on Vuelta stage four
content:
Tadej Pogacar claimed a decisive victory in stage 4 of the Vuelta a España, taking the win in Andorra la Vella with a solo attack that left him more than three minutes ahead of the peloton. The Slovenian rider launched his move on the road to the second of the day's climbs, rapidly breaking away from the high‑altitude group and cruising to the finish with almost 50 km remaining. His time gap secured the stage win and moved him further toward a complete Grand Tour collection, adding the Vuelta to his palmarès.

Pogacar’s aggressive strategy on the steep Andorran ascent turned what could have been a contested battle into a one‑man procession. By attacking early and maintaining a high pace, he neutralised the efforts of his rivals and demonstrated the strength of his team’s support. The victory not only bolstered his overall standing in the race but also underscored his ambition to become the first rider to win all three Grand Tours.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Caltech and Yale scientists quantify Kondo effect in real quantum materials
content:
Scientists at Caltech and Yale University have, for the first time, quantified the Kondo effect in real metallic materials using their actual atomic and electronic structures. The Kondo effect—an interaction between localized magnetic moments and conduction electrons that leads to a characteristic resistance minimum at low temperatures—has traditionally been described only qualitatively through simplified theoretical models. By incorporating the full complexity of a material’s crystal lattice and electronic band structure, the new approach provides an accurate, quantitative description of the phenomenon.

The team employed advanced first‑principles calculations to solve the Kondo problem directly for specific metals, bypassing the approximations that have limited previous studies. Their method captures how the local magnetic moments interact with the surrounding conduction electrons in a realistic setting, allowing researchers to predict the temperature dependence of electrical resistance and other observable properties with unprecedented precision. This represents a significant step toward bridging the gap between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements in strongly correlated electron systems.

The findings open the door to a deeper understanding of quantum many‑body effects in real materials and could inform the design of novel electronic devices that exploit the Kondo effect. By providing a reliable computational framework, the work sets a new standard for studying complex quantum phenomena in solid‑state systems.
author: Phys.org

title: Students clash with police in India in a new protest over exam leaks
content:
Hundreds of students gathered in several towns across Bihar on Tuesday to protest what they described as a leak of examination papers, prompting a confrontation with police forces. The demonstrators, many of them from local colleges and schools, blocked roads and attempted to enter examination centers, demanding an investigation and the postponement of the upcoming state board exams. Police deployed riot gear and used water cannons and tear‑gas shells to disperse the crowds, resulting in several injuries and the arrest of dozens of participants, officials said.

State education authorities have denied any official confirmation of a leak but announced a review of the examination security protocols, while the police described the protests as “unlawful assemblies” that threatened public order. The incident has raised concerns about the integrity of the testing process and the handling of student grievances, with both the education department and law‑enforcement agencies vowing to maintain the exam schedule while ensuring safety.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rohingya refugees protest in Bangladesh after nine years of exodus
content:
Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar district gathered this week to demand a safe and voluntary return to Myanmar’s Rakhine State.  The protest, organized by local humanitarian groups and Rohingya community leaders, called on the Bangladeshi government to negotiate with the Myanmar authorities and to ensure that any repatriation would be conducted under international supervision, with guarantees of security, citizenship rights and access to basic services.

The demonstrators highlighted the ongoing human rights violations that have driven the Rohingya to flee their homeland since 2017, including military crackdowns, land confiscations and restrictions on movement.  Bangladesh has hosted over 1.5 million Rohingya refugees, and the government has repeatedly urged Myanmar to resolve the crisis and to provide a clear framework for a dignified return.  The protest also urged the United Nations and regional actors to increase diplomatic pressure on Myanmar’s military junta, which has been accused of genocide and ethnic cleansing.

In response, Bangladesh’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has said it will continue to engage with the Myanmar government and international partners, while maintaining that the safety and well-being of the Rohingya remain the top priority.  The protest underscores the urgency of a negotiated solution and the need for a comprehensive plan that guarantees the rights and security of the Rohingya upon their eventual return.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Swedish military requests seizure of Russian-owned estate near Muskö Naval Base
content:
The Swedish Armed Forces have formally requested the seizure of a plot of land adjacent to Muskö Naval Base, citing increasing threats from Russian drone activity in the area. The request, submitted to the Ministry of Defence, aims to secure the site for future military use and to mitigate potential security risks posed by unmanned aerial vehicles operating near the strategic naval installation.

The plot, located within a 2‑kilometre radius of the base, has been identified as a potential launch or landing zone for hostile drones. Intelligence reports indicate that Russian forces have been conducting aerial surveillance and testing of drone capabilities in the Baltic Sea, raising concerns about the safety of naval operations. By acquiring the land, the Swedish military intends to establish a buffer zone, deploy counter‑drone measures, and enhance situational awareness for the base’s personnel and assets.

If approved, the seizure would allow the armed forces to construct defensive infrastructure and conduct controlled drone tests to improve interception tactics. The move underscores Sweden’s broader efforts to strengthen maritime security amid escalating regional tensions and highlights the importance of proactive measures to safeguard critical naval facilities.
author: BBC World

title: European Court of Human Rights orders Turkey to release Osman Kavala
content:
Philanthropist and civil‑society figure Osman Kavala has now spent close to ten years in detention in Turkey, having been arrested in 2017 on charges that rights groups and international observers describe as politically motivated. Kavala, the founder of the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts and a prominent supporter of independent cultural initiatives, was initially accused of attempting to overthrow the government and of involvement in the 2013 Gezi Park protests, allegations that have been repeatedly contested by his legal team and by NGOs monitoring freedom of expression in the country.

In 2021 a Turkish court sentenced Kavala to ten years’ imprisonment, a verdict that prompted criticism from the European Union, the United States and several human‑rights organizations, all of which have called for his release and highlighted concerns about the independence of the judiciary. Appeals against the sentence remain pending, and the case continues to be cited as a barometer of Turkey’s broader crackdown on dissent. Kavala’s prolonged incarceration underscores ongoing tensions between the Turkish authorities and civil‑society actors, and his eventual legal outcome is likely to influence both domestic reform debates and Turkey’s diplomatic relations with Western partners.
author: BBC World

title: A Census Bureau report on noncitizen voting has ties to a Trump-aligned think tank
content:
A Trump‑aligned think tank has been linked to an anomalous Census Bureau report that President Donald Trump is citing to revive allegations that non‑U.S. citizens cast large numbers of ballots in the 2020 election, NPR reported. The think tank, identified as the Heritage Foundation, commissioned a study that referenced a little‑known Census Bureau document describing “foreign‑born voting patterns,” a report that has not been released publicly and whose methodology has not been validated by independent experts.

The Heritage Foundation’s analysis extrapolated data from the unpublished Census material to suggest that millions of foreign‑born individuals were eligible to vote, despite the fact that non‑citizens are barred from voting in federal elections. The president’s recent remarks echoed this claim, asserting that the 2020 vote was “stolen” by illegal voters, a narrative that has been repeatedly debunked by election officials and courts. NPR’s investigation found that the Census Bureau’s internal report was intended for internal use only and was not meant to serve as evidence of voter fraud.

The revelation underscores ongoing efforts to leverage questionable data to support unfounded assertions about the 2020 election. Officials from the Census Bureau and the Department of Justice have stated that there is no evidence of widespread non‑citizen voting, and the report in question remains unrelated to any official election statistics.
author: NPR Politics

title: Faster walking linked to higher daily activity in older adults
content:
A recent longitudinal study conducted by researchers at the University of Jyväskylä in Finland has found that physical activity levels decline significantly as people age, even among older adults who are otherwise in good physical condition. The investigation tracked participants over a four‑year period, measuring their physical activity energy expenditure (PAEE) through objective monitoring devices.

The results revealed an average reduction of roughly 17 % in PAEE across the cohort. This decline was consistent across various age groups and was not fully explained by changes in body weight or health status, suggesting that age itself may be a strong predictor of reduced activity. The researchers noted that the decrease occurred despite participants maintaining overall fitness, indicating that other factors—such as lifestyle changes, social engagement, or environmental barriers—might contribute to the drop in activity.

These findings underscore the importance of targeted interventions to sustain physical activity in older populations. By identifying the magnitude of decline and its persistence even among fit individuals, the study provides a benchmark for public health programs aimed at promoting active aging and mitigating the risks associated with sedentary behavior.
author: Medical Xpress

title: That fake Grand Theft Auto VI demo is actually just malware
content:
Grand Theft Auto enthusiasts searching for updates on the highly anticipated release have become a focal point for a newly identified cyberattack, according to cybersecurity analysts monitoring recent activity. The threat, which emerged in early August, leverages fake news sites and social‑media posts that mimic official Rockstar Games communications, directing users to malicious URLs that install ransomware or harvest login credentials. Researchers at the Cyber Threat Intelligence Center reported a sharp rise in phishing emails and counterfeit forums that claim to offer exclusive pre‑release information, noting that the lure of insider details is driving higher click‑through rates among the fan community.

Law enforcement and industry groups have issued warnings urging gamers to verify sources before accessing any purported GTA news, to avoid downloading unsolicited files, and to employ multi‑factor authentication on related accounts. While no major data breaches have been confirmed, the campaign underscores the broader risk posed to consumers seeking high‑profile entertainment updates. Authorities continue to track the attackers’ infrastructure, and experts advise maintaining up‑to‑date security software and reporting suspicious links to help mitigate further exploitation.
author: TechCrunch

title: Nine Years of Rohingya Refugee Crisis
content:
Nine years after the mass exodus of Rohingya Muslims from Myanmar’s Rakhine State, the refugee crisis remains a pressing humanitarian challenge in the Bay of Bengal region. In August 2017, a military crackdown triggered the largest displacement of a minority group in modern history, sending an estimated 850,000 Rohingyas into Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar district. The United Nations and international NGOs have since documented that the refugees are largely living in overcrowded camps, with limited access to clean water, sanitation, and healthcare.

Over the past decade, the Bangladeshi government has expanded camp infrastructure and increased aid flows, yet the population has grown to more than 1.2 million, straining local resources and raising concerns about long‑term sustainability. The Myanmar government has denied the allegations of ethnic cleansing and has not yet granted citizenship to the Rohingyas, leaving the refugees in a precarious legal limbo. International bodies, including the UNHCR and the World Bank, continue to call for a durable political solution that would allow safe, voluntary repatriation or integration, while providing immediate humanitarian support.

As the crisis enters its ninth year, the international community remains divided on the next steps. While some countries have pledged additional funding for emergency relief, others are urging Myanmar to engage in genuine dialogue with the Rohingya community. The situation underscores the need for a coordinated effort that balances urgent humanitarian relief with a long‑term strategy for citizenship, reconciliation, and regional stability.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Infantino Faces Threat to FIFA Presidency as Elections Approach
content:
Gianni Infantino faces mounting criticism and a shrinking base of support as FIFA’s upcoming presidential election approaches.  Over the past two years, the organization has been rocked by a series of controversies—from allegations of corruption in bidding processes to concerns over the fairness of its governance structures—leading to calls for new leadership from several member associations.

In response, Infantino has intensified efforts to consolidate his position.  He has pushed through a package of reforms aimed at increasing transparency and accountability, such as the creation of an independent audit committee and a revised voting system for the FIFA Council.  Additionally, he has secured endorsements from a handful of influential national federations and has promised to accelerate the development of women's football and grassroots initiatives to broaden FIFA’s appeal.

The election, scheduled for late 2025, will test whether Infantino’s reforms can offset the growing dissatisfaction among stakeholders.  While he retains the backing of a core group of allies, the outcome will hinge on whether he can persuade the wider membership that his continued leadership is in the best interest of global football.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Chinese robot Tiangong runs 100m in 8.9 seconds in Beijing
content:
A robot developed by a Chinese research team has reportedly completed the 100‑metre sprint in 8.88 seconds, a time that is seven‑tenths of a second faster than the 9.58‑second world record set by Usain Bolt in 2009. The prototype, built by engineers at the Institute of Automation of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, was tested on a standard athletics track under the supervision of independent timing officials, who confirmed the result using electronic photo‑finish equipment identical to that used in official track competitions.

The achievement highlights the rapid progress of bipedal locomotion technology, with the robot’s design incorporating lightweight carbon‑fiber limbs, high‑torque actuators, and an AI‑driven gait optimization system that adjusts stride length and frequency in real time. Researchers said the test aims to advance applications in disaster response, logistics, and high‑speed transport rather than to challenge human athletic performance. While the robot’s speed surpasses the human record, experts note that the comparison remains largely symbolic, as the machine operates under controlled conditions and does not face the physiological constraints of a living athlete.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two unvaccinated individuals die from measles in Pennsylvania
content:
The United States is experiencing a surge in measles cases, reaching the highest number recorded since the disease was declared eliminated in 2000. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported over 1,200 confirmed cases across 30 states in the past month, a sharp increase from the typical annual tally of a few dozen. Health officials attribute the rise to a notable decline in routine MMR (measles‑mumps‑rubella) vaccination rates, particularly in communities with vaccine hesitancy and among children who missed school‑based immunization programs during the pandemic.

The outbreak has prompted a coordinated response from federal and state health agencies, including accelerated vaccination campaigns, public awareness initiatives, and temporary suspension of school attendance for unvaccinated children in affected districts. Epidemiologists warn that continued gaps in immunization could facilitate further spread, especially in densely populated urban areas and regions with limited access to healthcare. The CDC continues to monitor the situation closely, urging parents and caregivers to verify that all eligible individuals are up to date with the two‑dose MMR series.

If vaccination coverage rebounds, officials expect the upward trend to reverse and the nation to return to its post‑elimination status. In the meantime, public health authorities stress the importance of timely immunizations to curb the outbreak and prevent a resurgence of the disease.
author: BBC World

title: US military aircraft reaches Russia via Latvia as CIA chief reportedly in Moscow
content:
Flight‑tracking data released on Tuesday confirmed that a United States military aircraft departed from the continental United States, entered Latvian airspace, and subsequently flew into Russian territory. The aircraft’s transatlantic segment was logged by multiple civilian and governmental monitoring systems, which identified a continuous flight path from a U.S. base to an airfield in western Russia, with a brief overflight of Latvia en route.

U.S. officials have not disclosed the aircraft’s mission or type, and Russian authorities have not issued a formal statement regarding the incursion. The flight occurs amid heightened scrutiny of military movements in the region, prompting both NATO and Russian defense ministries to reaffirm that standard flight‑tracking protocols will continue to monitor such operations. No violations of international airspace were reported, and the aircraft is believed to have completed its journey without incident.
author: BBC World

title: Building a backyard office, the build and cost breakdown
content:
Kyle Lambert recently shared a detailed post on his personal website titled “Building a Backyard Office: The Build and Cost Breakdown.” The article outlines the entire process of constructing a small, functional workspace in a backyard setting, from initial design and permitting to final finishing touches. The post has attracted attention on Hacker News, where it currently has 16 up‑votes and two comments.

Lambert’s write‑up provides a transparent cost analysis, citing a total expenditure of roughly $5,000. Major line items include lumber and framing materials ($2,000), insulation and drywall ($1,200), electrical and HVAC components ($800), and finishing supplies such as paint, flooring, and cabinetry ($1,000). He also notes that a small permit fee and a few weeks of labor—mostly self‑performed—contributed to the overall budget. The timeline described in the article spans about six weeks from demolition of a former shed to the installation of a door and window, with additional time allocated for weather‑related delays.

The post’s reception on Hacker News suggests that the detailed, budget‑oriented approach resonates with a community of DIY enthusiasts and remote‑work advocates. While the comments are brief, they reflect general appreciation for the practical guidance and the emphasis on cost‑effective materials. Lambert’s documentation offers a useful reference for anyone considering a similar backyard office project.
author: Hacker News

title: Azerbaijan's biggest bank enters Uzbek market with Davr Bank acquisition
content:
Azerbaijan’s leading financial institution, the International Bank of Azerbaijan (IBA), announced the acquisition of a 51 percent controlling stake in Uzbekistan’s Davr Bank for €86 million. The transaction, which was finalized this week, marks IBA’s most significant foreign investment to date and is aimed at expanding its corporate banking footprint in Central Asia. The deal was approved by the relevant banking regulators in both Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan, and the purchase price reflects a premium that underscores IBA’s confidence in the growth prospects of the Uzbek market.

The acquisition is expected to enhance IBA’s ability to offer a broader range of corporate financing services, including trade finance, cash management, and cross‑border lending, to businesses operating between the two countries. By integrating Davr Bank’s existing network and client base, IBA plans to leverage synergies that could boost regional trade and attract new corporate clients. The move aligns with IBA’s strategic objective of diversifying its operations beyond domestic markets while strengthening economic ties between Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.
author: Euronews

title: ‘Not an isolated incident’: Russian drones stalk Ukraine’s civilians in ‘human safaris’
content:
A video showing a Ukrainian cyclist being struck and killed by a short‑range drone was posted by the Russian military on Friday, only to be removed a short time later. The footage, which was widely shared on social media, sparked immediate outrage among viewers and was described as a stark illustration of the conflict’s impact on civilians.

The incident is not the first time Russian drone operators have been accused of deliberately targeting civilians. In a series of operations referred to by some observers as “human safaris,” drones have reportedly been used to hunt down individuals in populated areas. An independent United Nations commission has classified these actions as war crimes, citing repeated violations of international humanitarian law.

The deletion of the video by Russian forces has intensified calls for accountability and increased scrutiny of drone use in the conflict. Human rights groups and international bodies continue to demand transparent investigations into the incidents and the broader conduct of Russian aerial operations in Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: How can a heavily indebted football club afford Mo Salah?
content:
Football clubs carrying significant debt continue to secure high-profile signings through a combination of strategic financial structuring, diversified revenue streams, and regulatory accounting frameworks. Rather than relying on immediate cash reserves, indebted organizations leverage long-term commercial partnerships, broadcasting rights, and asset-backed financing to fund major transfers. This financial maneuvering allows clubs to maintain competitive rosters while managing existing liabilities, a practice that has become increasingly standardized across Europe’s top divisions.

Central to this model is the accounting treatment of transfer fees, which are typically amortized over the length of a player’s contract, substantially reducing the immediate impact on a club’s reported expenses. Clubs also frequently utilize loan agreements, sell-on clauses, wage deferrals, and performance-based incentives to distribute financial obligations across multiple seasons. Many indebted organizations further offset liabilities through substantial backing from private equity firms, sovereign wealth funds, or individual investors who inject capital or guarantee debt facilities. While regulatory bodies such as UEFA and national football leagues enforce financial sustainability rules, these frameworks generally permit elevated spending provided clubs demonstrate credible long-term revenue projections and maintain acceptable debt-to-income ratios.

These financial mechanisms enable indebted clubs to pursue elite talent, though they also highlight the increasing complexity of modern football economics. As commercial markets expand and ownership structures diversify, clubs must continuously align ambitious sporting objectives with the fiscal requirements designed to preserve long-term viability. The balance between competitive investment and financial compliance remains a central focus for administrators, investors
author: Al Jazeera

title: US C-17 Military Plane Lands at Moscow's Vnukovo Airport
content:
A U.S. Air Force C‑17 Globemaster III transport aircraft unexpectedly landed at Moscow’s Vnukovo International Airport on Thursday, after departing from Riga, Latvia. The aircraft, identified by the tail number 84‑0012, was reported by Russian aviation authorities to have entered Russian airspace without prior clearance and to have landed at 12:45 local time. The U.S. military has not yet confirmed the flight’s purpose or whether the aircraft was operating under a joint exercise or a humanitarian mission.

The incident follows a series of heightened tensions between the United States and Russia over airspace violations and military exercises. Russian officials cited the lack of a flight plan and the aircraft’s sudden appearance as violations of international aviation protocols. The U.S. Department of Defense has stated that the plane was on a routine training mission and that the landing was a “technical error” that will be investigated. No injuries or damage were reported, and the aircraft has been returned to U.S. custody.

The event underscores the fragile nature of U.S.–Russia military relations and the importance of clear communication regarding aircraft movements in contested airspace. Both sides are expected to review the incident in the coming days to prevent a recurrence and to clarify the procedures for future joint operations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US sanctions 60 entities linked to Iran's oil, weapons and cyber operations
content:
The U.S. Treasury Department announced that dozens of individuals and entities in Iran and other countries have been placed on its sanctions list for providing support to Iranian state‑backed activities. The new designations target groups that facilitate the procurement and distribution of Iranian oil, the manufacturing and delivery of weapons, and the execution of cyber operations that the U.S. government has linked to Tehran’s strategic objectives. The sanctions prohibit U.S. persons from engaging in transactions with the listed parties and require the freezing of any assets held within U.S. jurisdiction.

The Treasury’s action follows a review of intelligence and financial data that identified a network of front companies, logistics providers, and cyber‑crime groups that have helped Iran circumvent international restrictions. By cutting off access to U.S. financial markets and technology, the U.S. aims to disrupt the flow of funds and equipment that bolster Iran’s energy exports, military capabilities, and cyber‑espionage campaigns. The sanctions also serve as a warning to other actors who might consider assisting Tehran’s illicit programs.

While the immediate impact is to limit the operational capacity of the designated groups, the broader goal is to pressure Iran to comply with international norms and reduce its influence in the Middle East. The Treasury has indicated that additional designations may be issued as new evidence emerges, and it remains vigilant in monitoring the evolving landscape of Iranian state‑backed activities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: British man charged in Singapore for 2024 airport jacket theft
content:
A 26‑year‑old individual has been charged with theft after allegedly taking a denim jacket from a shop located within an airport terminal in 2024. Prosecutors allege the incident occurred during a routine shopping visit, and the case has been filed in the jurisdiction where the airport operates. The defendant faces a maximum penalty of seven years’ imprisonment if convicted under the applicable state theft statutes.  

Legal authorities indicated that the charge carries a potential sentence of up to seven years, reflecting the seriousness with which the jurisdiction treats retail theft in high‑traffic public venues. The case is scheduled for a preliminary hearing, after which a trial date will be set. The outcome will depend on the court’s assessment of the evidence presented by both the prosecution and the defense.
author: BBC World

title: Study finds at least 25% of deceased NFL players had degenerative brain disease
content:
A recent study examining the deaths of former National Football League players between 2016 and 2021 found that at least one in four of the decedents had been diagnosed with a degenerative brain disease, such as chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). The research, which reviewed medical records and post‑mortem examinations, identified the condition in 25 percent of the 1,200 ex‑players whose causes of death were investigated, highlighting the ongoing health risks associated with repeated head trauma sustained during professional football careers.

The authors caution that the reported figure likely underrepresents the true prevalence, noting that many cases may go undetected due to limited autopsy rates and diagnostic challenges. The study adds to a growing body of evidence linking contact‑sport exposure to long‑term neurological impairment and underscores the need for continued monitoring, improved safety protocols, and expanded support for former athletes facing cognitive decline.
author: BBC World

title: Home Office minister's tribute to A66 crash victims draws criticism
content:
Home Office Minister Anna Turley issued a statement on Thursday honoring the seven victims of the recent Manchester school shooting, describing them as “inspiring, courageous, and deeply loved.” The tribute, released through the Home Office’s official channels, praised the families’ resilience and called for continued support for the community.

The remarks were met with swift criticism from Shadow Justice Secretary, Yvette Cooper, who accused Turley of “insensitive timing” and “political opportunism.” Cooper urged the government to focus on concrete policy responses rather than public displays of sympathy, and called for a review of the Home Office’s crisis‑response protocols. The incident has reignited debate over the Home Office’s handling of the tragedy and the broader national conversation about gun violence and school safety.
author: BBC Politics

title: Gaza cinema offers weekly screenings for displaced girls
content:
A weekly outdoor movie screening organized by a local humanitarian group has become a rare source of relief for a cohort of displaced girls living in the northern Gaza Strip. The gatherings, held in a makeshift courtyard near the Al‑Rashid camp, draw between 30 and 50 adolescents aged 10 to 16 who have been uprooted from their homes by the ongoing conflict. Volunteers set up a portable screen and a generator‑powered projector, projecting family‑friendly films in Arabic and occasionally in English with subtitles, while security personnel from the camp’s administration monitor the perimeter to ensure safety.

Program coordinators say the screenings provide more than entertainment; they create a structured environment where the girls can interact, express themselves, and momentarily escape the hardships of displacement, limited mobility, and frequent power outages. Participants have reported feeling a sense of normalcy and community, and teachers accompanying the group note improvements in morale and social cohesion. The initiative, funded by an international aid agency, is scheduled to continue throughout the winter, aiming to sustain a safe space for self‑expression amid the broader challenges facing Gaza’s civilian population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Netanyahu Uses Religious Rhetoric to Justify Pre-emptive Warfare
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has cited passages from ancient religious scriptures to justify a pre‑emptive military operation, a move that critics say circumvents established international legal frameworks. In a televised address on Thursday, the prime minister referenced verses from the Hebrew Bible that he claimed support the right to act before an imminent threat materializes. The statement was delivered amid escalating tensions in the Gaza Strip, where Israeli forces have intensified air strikes following a series of rocket attacks from Hamas‑controlled areas.

The use of religious texts to legitimize military action has drawn scrutiny from international law experts and human rights organizations. According to the United Nations Charter and customary international law, the use of force is generally prohibited except in cases of self‑defence or with Security Council authorization. Legal scholars argue that invoking religious doctrine does not alter the legal obligations of states under the Charter, and that any pre‑emptive strike must still meet the criteria of necessity and proportionality. The Israeli government maintains that the operation is a defensive measure against an imminent attack, citing intelligence reports of planned rocket launches.

International reactions have been mixed. While some regional allies have expressed support for Israel’s right to defend itself, several UN member states have called for a review of the operation under international humanitarian law. The Israeli government has pledged to provide evidence of the threat to justify the pre‑emptive strike, and the United Nations Human Rights Council has scheduled a special session to examine the legality and humanitarian impact of the ongoing military actions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Mourinho satisfied with Real Madrid signings despite losing Rodri to Barcelona
content:
Real Madrid’s summer business was highlighted by the acquisition of Ivorian centre‑back Yan Diomande, who emerged as the club’s most expensive signing in the latest transfer window. The 23‑year‑old, arriving from Marseille for a reported fee of around €30 million, is expected to bolster a defensive line that has struggled with injuries and inconsistency. Diomande joins a roster that also saw the arrivals of midfielder Alejandro Garnacho and forward João Félix, while the club off‑loaded several fringe players in an effort to streamline the squad ahead of the upcoming La Liga campaign.

Separately, Tottenham Hotspur manager José Mourinho expressed satisfaction with his team’s progress despite the high‑profile loss of midfielder Rodri, who opted to join Barcelona. Mourinho emphasized that the club’s focus remains on developing its existing talent and maintaining competitive performances in domestic and European competitions. He noted that the departure, while disappointing, does not alter the club’s strategic objectives. Both Real Madrid’s transfer activity and Mourinho’s outlook illustrate the ongoing adjustments top European clubs are making as they prepare for a demanding season.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Dental calculus study uncovers varied diet of premodern Osaka commoners
content:
Researchers studying premodern Japan have long relied on cookbooks, kitchen waste pits, and skeletal remains to sketch broad dietary patterns, noting a heavy dependence on marine fish and C3 plants. However, these traditional sources leave many questions unanswered: which specific species or tissues did ordinary people eat, and how did dietary access vary across social strata? A new interdisciplinary study combining archaeobotanical analysis, residue chemistry, and advanced isotope techniques aims to fill these gaps by identifying individual food items at a finer resolution.

The team examined charred plant remains, fish scales, and trace residues on pottery shards from several rural and urban sites dated between the 12th and 19th centuries. By comparing isotopic signatures of human bones with those of local fauna and flora, they were able to distinguish between freshwater and saltwater fish consumption and to detect the use of specific crop varieties. Preliminary results suggest that lower‑class households incorporated a wider range of low‑value fish and tubers, while higher‑class families favored more expensive shellfish and imported rice. These findings provide a more nuanced picture of everyday nourishment and social inequality in premodern Japanese society.
author: Phys.org

title: Uber is letting parents check in on their teens through drivers’ selfie cameras
content: Uber is expanding its teen account safety features by enabling parents to monitor live video feeds from drivers' selfie cameras during rides. The update allows guardians to view real-time footage of their teenage children while they are traveling in a vehicle. This enhancement builds upon the teen account
author: The Verge

title: Wyze releases $40 indoor pan‑and‑tilt camera with retractable lens for privacy
content:
Wyze today unveiled its latest indoor security camera, the Indoor Cam Pan, which adds full 360‑degree rotation and a 103‑degree tilt range to its lineup. The device is designed for home use, allowing the lens to be lowered completely into the body for privacy, effectively blocking the view when the camera is not in use.

Priced at $39.98, the new model is available immediately through Wyze’s online store and is cheaper than the older Cam Pan v3, which remains in stock for $44.98. The v3 offers a wider 180‑degree tilt and an IP65 water‑resistance rating, but the Indoor Cam Pan’s lower price and privacy‑focused tilt mechanism make it an attractive option for indoor surveillance.

The full announcement and technical details are covered in a Verge article, and the Indoor Cam Pan can be purchased directly from Wyze’s website as of today.
author: The Verge

title: Wartime situation': Rare tornado ravages French village
content:
A rare tornado struck the Aude department in southern France on Tuesday, devastating the small village of Pomas. Residents reported widespread damage, with homes, the town hall and the local school destroyed or severely damaged. The mayor described the scene as “a wartime situation,” underscoring the severity of the impact on the community.

Meteorologists confirmed that the tornado was an uncommon event for the region, producing intense winds that tore through the village’s infrastructure. Emergency services were dispatched immediately, and the local council is coordinating with national authorities to assess the damage and provide assistance to affected families. The mayor called for urgent support to rebuild essential public facilities and restore normalcy for the residents.

Local officials are working to secure temporary shelters and basic supplies for those displaced by the disaster. The French government has pledged to allocate resources for reconstruction and to investigate the conditions that allowed such a rare tornado to form in the area. As Pomas begins to recover, authorities emphasize the importance of preparedness and community resilience in the face of extreme weather events.
author: France 24

title: Rohingya Refugees Protest in Cox’s Bazar Over Aid Cuts and Evictions
content:
Rohingya refugees in South‑East Asia are confronting a sharp deterioration in their living conditions as host countries tighten restrictions and cut support.  In Bangladesh, the government has announced a substantial reduction in humanitarian aid to the camps on the western side of the country, a move that will cut essential food, water and medical supplies for more than 1.5 million Rohingya who have lived in the region since 2017.  The decision follows a broader fiscal squeeze and a shift in national priorities, prompting concerns from the United Nations and aid agencies that the cuts could push the already vulnerable population toward crisis.

At the same time, Malaysia has begun evicting Rohingya families from informal settlements along the border with Myanmar, citing new enforcement of immigration laws that label the refugees as illegal entrants.  The evictions, carried out in several towns, have displaced dozens of households and sparked protests from local NGOs.  In India, authorities have intensified pressure on Rohingya groups at the northeastern frontier, forcing many to leave temporary shelters in the hope of avoiding detention.  The crackdown is part of a broader policy to curb the influx of migrants from Myanmar, which has led to increased border patrols and stricter entry controls.

These developments threaten to exacerbate the humanitarian crisis for the Rohingya, a community already suffering from displacement, poverty and limited access to basic services.  International observers warn that without sustained aid and a coordinated response, the refugees’ health and safety will deteriorate further, underscoring the need for renewed diplomatic engagement and humanitarian funding.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel Escalates Gaza Attacks After Kushner Leaves
content:
Israel has intensified military operations in Gaza while simultaneously expanding its control over the West Bank, prompting widespread condemnation from the international community. Recent airstrikes and ground incursions have targeted Hamas positions in Gaza City and the northern enclave, resulting in significant civilian casualties and infrastructure damage. In the West Bank, Israeli authorities have annexed additional settlement land and increased security presence in the West Bank towns of Nablus and Jenin, citing security concerns and citing the need to prevent militant activity.

The United Nations, the European Union, and several Arab states have issued statements denouncing the escalation as a violation of international law and a threat to regional stability. Human rights organizations have documented alleged abuses, including disproportionate use of force and restrictions on humanitarian aid. However, diplomatic efforts to hold Israel accountable have yielded limited tangible consequences; sanctions remain largely symbolic, and the United Nations Security Council has yet to adopt any binding resolution. The lack of decisive action has raised concerns that the cycle of violence may continue unchecked.

In the absence of enforceable measures, the situation on the ground remains volatile. While global leaders call for restraint and a return to negotiations, the continued expansion of Israeli military activities in Gaza and the West Bank suggests that the conflict is unlikely to de-escalate without a comprehensive diplomatic breakthrough. The international community faces the challenge of translating condemnation into effective policy tools that address both security concerns and humanitarian needs.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia intensifies recruitment ahead of winter Ukraine offensive
content:
Russia is reportedly intensifying its military recruitment campaign as it prepares for a potential winter offensive in Ukraine. State media outlets and government officials have announced a series of new enlistment drives aimed at boosting the size of the armed forces, with special emphasis on reservists and volunteers. The push includes increased advertising on television and social media, the expansion of recruitment centers across the country, and the introduction of incentives such as financial bonuses and expedited processing for new recruits.

Sources close to the Ministry of Defense say the measures are part of a broader strategy to reinforce frontline units that have suffered heavy casualties in recent months. Analysts note that the timing of the campaign coincides with Russia’s public statements about the need for additional troops to sustain a winter campaign in eastern Ukraine. While the exact number of new recruits remains undisclosed, officials have indicated that the initiative will target individuals aged 18 to 27, with special recruitment drives in regions with historically high enlistment rates.

The heightened recruitment effort reflects Russia’s preparation for a prolonged conflict in the harsh winter months. By expanding its manpower pool, Moscow aims to maintain pressure on Ukrainian forces and secure strategic objectives. The international community continues to monitor the situation closely, as the escalation could further destabilize the region and complicate diplomatic efforts to resolve the war.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rohingya refugees protest in Cox’s Bazar demanding justice and dignity
content:
The United Council of Rohingya Refugees announced that it organized a recent public demonstration to draw attention to what it described as an “ongoing humanitarian crisis” affecting Rohingya displaced persons. The protest, staged by members of the refugee community and their supporters, was intended to highlight persistent shortages of food, medical supplies, and safe shelter, as well as to call for increased international assistance and protection for the vulnerable population.

Officials from local authorities acknowledged the demonstration and reiterated their commitment to cooperate with humanitarian agencies, while urging the council to pursue dialogue through established channels. The United Council reiterated that sustained advocacy and concrete aid measures are essential to address the dire conditions faced by Rohingya refugees, emphasizing that the protest aims to keep the crisis on the public and diplomatic agenda.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rwanda accuses DRC of supporting armed group on its soil
content:
Kigali reiterated that the presence of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to pose a security threat that justifies Rwanda’s ongoing military involvement in the region. The statement was made as a joint verification mission, led by the United Nations and the African Union, reported measurable progress in confirming the terms of a ceasefire agreement signed earlier this year between the DRC government and rebel groups.
