Hiltermann will focus on strengthening the Group’s work in the region, particularly on the Palestinian Authority (PA) and its institutions.

Hiltermann argues that the PA’s financial crisis is not a sudden emergency but a prolonged process of institutional and economic erosion. He notes that the Authority has already lost much of its ability to deliver essential services, pay public‑sector salaries in full, maintain infrastructure, and support education and health care. These deficits are compounded by settlement expansion, settler violence and Israeli restrictions, which together create a hostile environment for Palestinian governance and economic stability.

The combination of ongoing settlement activity, security restrictions and financial pressures poses a continuing threat to Palestinian institutions and economic life. Hiltermann’s assessment underscores the need for sustained international attention to the PA’s capacity challenges and the broader conditions that shape its future.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine MPs Approve New Defence Minister After Reshuffle
content:
Ukraine’s parliament approved a new defence minister on Wednesday, a month after a controversial reshuffle that saw the dismissal of the popular former minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The decision follows a public backlash that erupted when Fedorov was removed, with critics arguing that the move undermined civilian oversight of the armed forces amid the ongoing war with Russia.

The new appointment comes a day after Fedorov released a video statement in which he urged the government to resume elections that have been postponed due to the Russian invasion. His call for democratic renewal was met with mixed reactions, as some saw it as a necessary step toward restoring normalcy, while others feared it could destabilise an already fragile political environment. The parliament’s approval of the new minister is therefore seen as both a response to domestic pressure and a signal that Kyiv remains focused on maintaining a robust defence posture.

With the new defence minister taking office, Ukraine continues to navigate the dual challenge of sustaining its military campaigns against Russian forces and addressing internal demands for political reform. The appointment underscores the government’s attempt to balance strategic security needs with growing calls for democratic processes, a balancing act that will shape Ukraine’s political landscape in the coming months.
author: France 24

title: Turkey rejects Israel's claims after strike on Syrian air base
content:
Turkey on Wednesday rejected what it described as “untenable allegations” from Israel concerning Ankara’s military posture in Syria after Israeli jets struck the Abu al‑Duhur air base near Aleppo, close to the Turkish border. Israel said the strike was a response to intelligence indicating that Syria was about to allow Turkish forces to operate on its territory, a claim Turkey dismissed as baseless. The Israeli attack, which targeted the Syrian facility on Tuesday, prompted an official protest from the Turkish foreign ministry, which condemned the violation of Syrian sovereignty and warned against any escalation that could destabilise the region.

The United States also weighed in, with a senior envoy labeling the Israeli airstrike an “unnecessary escalation” and urging restraint from all parties. The incident adds to a series of cross‑border tensions involving Israel, Syria and Turkey, where each side has expressed concerns over security and the potential deployment of foreign troops. Observers note that the episode underscores the fragile security dynamics along the northern Syrian frontier, and diplomatic efforts are expected to focus on preventing further military confrontations.
author: France 24

title: Ukrainian anti-corruption probe targets Zelensky office after ex-defence minister urges elections
content:
Ukrainian anti‑corruption agencies announced on Wednesday that they have opened investigations into senior officials within President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s office. The probe comes a day after the country’s recently dismissed defence minister, Oleksiy Reznikov, publicly urged the scheduling of national elections despite the ongoing war with Russia, a move that has been described as a political distraction amid the conflict’s fifth year. The anti‑corruption bodies said the inquiries will focus on alleged abuses of power and financial misconduct, though they have not disclosed the identities of the officials under scrutiny.

The developments arrive at a sensitive moment for Kyiv, as the war effort continues to dominate the national agenda and international support. France 24’s International Affairs Editor Philip Turle noted that the investigations could further strain the president’s administration and shift attention away from military priorities. Authorities have pledged to conduct the inquiries transparently, emphasizing that anti‑corruption measures remain a core component of Ukraine’s governance even as it confronts external aggression.
author: France 24

title: Stable engineered human fibroblast growth factor created for therapeutic research
content:
A team of researchers has announced a breakthrough in protein engineering, reporting in the *Biophysical Journal* the creation of a stable, biologically active form of human fibroblast growth factor (FGF). The study details how the modified protein retains the key functional domains required for cell signaling while exhibiting markedly improved thermal stability and resistance to proteolytic degradation—issues that have historically limited the therapeutic use of FGF.

The enhanced FGF variant was engineered through targeted amino‑acid substitutions that preserve its receptor‑binding interface yet reduce conformational flexibility. In vitro assays demonstrated that the protein maintains its ability to stimulate fibroblast proliferation and to promote wound‑healing pathways, while also exhibiting antidiabetic activity by enhancing insulin sensitivity in cultured adipocytes. The authors suggest that this stabilized form could serve as a more reliable candidate for drug development, potentially enabling oral or topical formulations that were previously unfeasible.

If these findings translate to in vivo models, the new FGF construct could accelerate the development of treatments for chronic wounds and metabolic disorders. The research team plans to advance preclinical studies to evaluate safety, dosing, and delivery strategies, with the ultimate goal of moving toward clinical trials.
author: Phys.org

title: Aid workers under fire as drones reshape warfare
content:
The United Nations has issued a stark warning that aid workers are confronting a deadly and evolving threat as armed drones increasingly reshape battlefields worldwide, putting humanitarian teams more frequently in the line of fire. The warning, released by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, highlights that drones are being used by state and non‑state actors to target strategic positions, often at close range to civilian populations and aid convoys.

According to the UN report, drone strikes have risen by more than 30 % in the past three years across conflict zones in the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia. The report cites several incidents in which aid workers were injured or killed when drones targeted supply routes or medical facilities. The UN stresses that the small size and low cost of many modern drones make them difficult to detect and counter, creating new risks for field staff who must navigate contested areas to deliver essential services.

The UN is urging all parties to the conflicts to respect international humanitarian law and to adopt measures that protect civilians and aid workers. It has called for the establishment of clear protocols for drone use in populated areas and for the creation of safe corridors for humanitarian operations. The organization’s latest briefing underscores the urgent need for coordinated global action to mitigate the growing threat posed by armed drones to those providing relief in war‑torn regions.
author: UN News

title: Six tourists and pilot die in Kenya helicopter crash
content:
A recent aircraft accident has prompted an update from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Department, which told the BBC that the nationalities of the passengers involved have not yet been confirmed. The incident, which occurred earlier this week, involved a commercial flight that crashed shortly after take‑off, resulting in a number of casualties and injuries.

Investigators are still compiling passenger manifests and other records to determine the identities and nationalities of those on board. The department emphasized that the information is pending verification and that further details will be released as the inquiry progresses. Authorities are coordinating with airlines and immigration agencies to expedite the confirmation process.

Once the passenger nationalities are confirmed, the department will provide a comprehensive report to the public. In the meantime, officials are focusing on the ongoing investigation and on delivering accurate information to affected families and the media.
author: BBC World

title: Ukrainian man arrested in Croatia over alleged Nord Stream sabotage
content:
A man has been charged with involvement in the 2022 sabotage of offshore pipelines, authorities said. Prosecutors allege that he was one of the scuba divers who placed explosives on the pipelines, an act that caused significant disruption to the region’s energy infrastructure and prompted a multi‑agency investigation.

Law enforcement officials disclosed that the suspect was identified through forensic analysis of recovered explosive devices and underwater surveillance footage. He has been detained pending trial, and investigators continue to examine whether additional individuals participated in the operation. The case underscores ongoing concerns about the security of critical energy assets and the resources allocated to prevent similar attacks.
author: BBC World

title: Everyone wants clarity' over Man City charges, says Arsenal chief
content:
Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick has publicly addressed the ongoing investigation into Manchester City, which centers on more than 100 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations. The remarks arrive as the league’s independent commission continues its review of the extensive case, a matter that has drawn sustained attention from clubs, officials, and supporters throughout English football. Garlick’s comments highlight the broader institutional emphasis on preserving competitive integrity and ensuring consistent application of the competition’s financial frameworks.

The allegations against Manchester City encompass a range of financial governance issues, including historical reporting practices, sponsorship arrangements, and compliance with established Premier League rules. Speaking in his capacity as a senior club executive, Garlick stressed the necessity of a transparent and methodical investigative process, noting that
author: BBC Sport

title: Alaska primary puts Rep. Sara Kreiss‑Tomkins ahead in open governor’s race
content:
Alaska’s next governor will be chosen in a ranked‑choice election that follows a broad open primary held on Tuesday.  Term‑limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy’s seat has attracted more than a dozen candidates, all vying for the top four spots that will advance to the general election.  The state’s unique nonpartisan blanket primary system allows voters to select any candidate, regardless of party, and the four highest‑scoring candidates move on to the next round.

Among the field, Democratic former state senator Tom Begich has emerged as the front‑runner in recent polls, according to data released by the Alaska Public Opinion Institute.  Begich’s lead is notable given the diversity of candidates, which includes several independents and Republicans who are also in contention.  The ranked‑choice format means that if no candidate secures a majority of first‑choice votes, the lowest‑placed candidates are eliminated and their votes redistributed until a winner is determined.

The election will be a decisive moment for Alaska’s political future, as voters weigh the prospects of candidates from both major parties and independent contenders.  The outcome will set the tone for the state’s policy direction in the coming years, with particular attention to issues such as resource development, public safety, and the management of Alaska’s extensive natural resources.  As the campaign season progresses, the focus will shift to the general election, where the top four will compete for the governorship.
author: The Hill

title: Finnish study links higher coffee consumption to lower fat and higher muscle mass
content:
A new Finnish study suggests that coffee may offer more than a simple energy lift. Researchers found that individuals who drank more coffee had lower total and abdominal fat, greater muscle mass, and healthier metabolic markers, all while maintaining similar body mass indices compared with lighter drinkers.

The investigation also revealed that higher coffee intake was associated with reduced levels of specific amino acids that are linked to insulin resistance and an increased risk of type 2 diabetes. These biochemical changes point to a potential protective effect of coffee on metabolic health, beyond its well‑known stimulant properties.

Overall, the findings highlight coffee’s possible role in improving body composition and metabolic risk factors, underscoring the beverage’s broader health implications.
author: Science Daily

title: Pakistan Challenges Supreme Court Order to Transfer Imran Khan to Private Hospital
content:
The Supreme Court has ordered that the jailed former prime minister, who is currently serving a sentence for corruption, receive a medical examination at a public hospital. In response, the government has filed a review of the order, arguing that the former leader should instead be examined at a private or specialized medical facility that can provide more comprehensive care. The review cites concerns over the adequacy of public hospital resources and the need for a thorough assessment of the ex‑prime minister’s health status.

The government’s petition, submitted to the Court’s review panel, requests that the original directive be set aside and replaced with a new arrangement that allows the former prime minister to undergo examination at a facility equipped with advanced diagnostic equipment and specialist staff. It also highlights that the ex‑prime minister’s health condition has been a matter of public debate and that a more detailed evaluation is necessary for any potential medical leave or release. The Court has yet to schedule a hearing on the review, and the case remains pending.

If the review is granted, the former prime minister would be transferred to the requested private or specialized hospital for a comprehensive medical assessment. The decision will be closely watched by opposition parties and civil society groups, who have called for transparency and accountability in the treatment of high‑profile prisoners. The outcome of the review could set a precedent for how the judiciary handles medical examinations of incarcerated public officials.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine sees rise in violent forced military recruitment
content:
In the past month, the term “Busification” has entered the public discourse as a descriptor for a growing trend of individuals being forcibly taken onto public buses in several urban centers across the country. The practice, which involves coercing or abducting people onto transit vehicles, has been identified by local NGOs and investigative journalists as a form of street capture that is increasingly tied to abuse and corruption. The phenomenon has prompted a wave of concern among civil‑rights groups, who argue that it undermines public safety and erodes trust in municipal transport systems.

According to a report released by the Urban Justice Coalition, Busification incidents have risen by roughly 35 % since the start of the year, with the majority occurring in densely populated districts where bus routes intersect with informal markets and nightlife venues. The report documents cases in which victims are threatened or physically restrained before boarding, and it highlights a pattern of collusion between certain bus operators and local law‑enforcement officers. In several documented instances, drivers have been seen accepting bribes to allow the transport of abducted individuals, while police officers have been accused of turning a blind eye or actively facilitating the process. The coalition’s findings also reveal that victims often face subsequent exploitation, such as forced labor or debt bondage, further entangling the practice in a broader network of corruption.

City officials have responded by announcing an independent inquiry into the allegations and pledging to strengthen oversight of public transport operations. The mayor’s office has called for a review of licensing procedures for bus operators and has urged the police department to conduct targeted investigations into the alleged collusion. While the investigation is still underway, civil‑rights advocates are calling for immediate protective measures for at‑risk populations and for transparent reporting of any findings. The unfolding situation underscores the need for coordinated action to address the abuse and corruption that have come to define Busification.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UAE Imposes Trade Embargo on Iran Over Missile Incidents
content:
The United Arab Emirates announced today that it will impose an embargo on Iranian goods, citing a recent incident in which Iranian missiles were reportedly launched into UAE territory. In a statement released by the UAE Ministry of Economy, officials said the decision was taken to safeguard national security and to signal the country’s firm stance against any military aggression from Iran.

The embargo, which will target a range of Iranian products including petrochemicals, machinery and consumer goods, follows a series of escalating tensions between the two Gulf states. Tehran has denied responsibility for the missile launch, while the UAE has called for an international investigation and urged other Gulf Cooperation Council members to support its measures. The move is expected to add pressure on Iran’s already strained economy and could prompt further diplomatic engagement in the region.

UAE officials emphasized that the embargo is a temporary measure aimed at deterring further hostile acts and protecting the country’s citizens. They also urged the international community to monitor the situation closely and to work toward a peaceful resolution of the broader Iran‑UAE dispute. The announcement comes amid growing concerns over regional stability and the potential for wider conflict in the Persian Gulf.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gold mine collapse kills dozens in Central African Republic
content:
A collapse at a small mining site near the Cameroon border in the Central African Republic has left dozens dead, and rescue teams are still working to reach survivors. The incident occurred in a remote area of the eastern province, where informal gold mining is common. Preliminary reports from local authorities indicate that at least 35 people were trapped beneath the collapsed shaft, with several others injured.

The Central African Republic’s Ministry of Mines has coordinated with the national armed forces and local civil protection units to conduct a multi‑stage rescue operation. Heavy equipment, including hydraulic lifts and breathing apparatus, has been deployed to stabilize the site and extract victims. Humanitarian organizations have also been called in to provide medical assistance and emergency supplies to the affected communities. The region’s limited infrastructure and the remote location have complicated the response, but officials say the rescue effort is progressing steadily.

As of the latest update, rescue crews have managed to reach several trapped miners, but the total number of survivors remains uncertain. Authorities have urged the public to stay away from the site for safety reasons and are working to secure the area while continuing the search and recovery mission. The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns in the country’s informal mining sector, where inadequate safety measures frequently lead to accidents.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bus and truck crash in Brazil kills over 20 people
content:
Two vehicles collided in the early hours of Wednesday morning, prompting a rapid response from local emergency services. Police arrived at the scene shortly after the crash was reported, securing the area and providing assistance to any individuals involved. At this time, officials have not identified the factors that led to the collision, and no preliminary cause has been established.

Investigators are conducting a thorough examination of the wreckage, reviewing surveillance footage, and interviewing witnesses to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. Traffic on the affected roadway was temporarily rerouted while authorities completed their assessment, and normal flow resumed once the site was cleared. The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities have indicated that further details will be released as they become available.
author: BBC World

title: Israeli army launches criminal probe into death of 5‑year‑old Palestinian girl in Gaza
content:
A five‑year‑old girl in Gaza City spent several hours on the telephone with emergency responders before her body was recovered days later, officials said. The incident, which occurred in 2024 amid ongoing hostilities in the enclave, was reported by local health authorities after paramedics were unable to reach the child in time despite continuous communication.

Authorities indicated that the child had been trapped in a residential area that had been struck, prompting the prolonged call for assistance. Paramedics arrived on scene but were unable to extract her before she succumbed to her injuries; her remains were retrieved several days after the initial emergency call. The case has been added to the growing list of civilian casualties documented by humanitarian agencies operating in Gaza, and officials continue to document and investigate the circumstances surrounding each incident.
author: BBC World

title: Israel issues tender for 1,200 housing units in contested E1 settlement area
content:
The Israeli government has issued a public tender for the construction of more than 1,200 housing units in the East Jerusalem area known as E1. The tender, announced by the Ministry of Housing and Construction, calls for developers to submit proposals for residential projects that will be built on land earmarked for the expansion of Israeli settlements. The project is part of a broader plan to increase the Israeli population in the area, a move that has drawn criticism from international bodies and Palestinian authorities.

E1 is a highly contested zone, situated between the Old City of Jerusalem and the Israeli settlement of Ma'ale Adumim. The United Nations, the European Union, and several Arab states have repeatedly described the settlement expansion in E1 as illegal under international law, citing the Fourth Geneva Convention. Israel, however, maintains that the land is disputed and that the development is a legitimate exercise of its sovereign rights. The tender process has been opened to both domestic and foreign developers, with the government stating that the projects will include a mix of private and public housing.

The announcement marks the latest step in the Israeli administration’s push to formalize settlement activity in East Jerusalem. While the government frames the initiative as a domestic housing solution, the international community continues to view the E1 expansion as a violation of the established legal framework governing occupied territories. The outcome of the tender will likely influence future diplomatic negotiations and the ongoing debate over the status of Jerusalem.
author: Al Jazeera

title: The everyday tech I use to track my corgi
content:
Apple’s AirTag, first marketed as a convenient way to keep tabs on keys, wallets, and luggage, is finding a new niche among pet owners. By attaching the small, waterproof device to a collar, owners can leverage Apple’s Find My network to locate their animals if they wander off or become lost. The technology, which uses Bluetooth and U‑1 chip proximity sensing, turns every Apple device into a potential beacon that can relay a pet’s position to the owner’s iPhone.

One user, who keeps a corgi named Jelly, has already installed an AirTag in a silicone holder on her dog’s collar. Though she has never had to use the tracker to retrieve Jelly, she describes it as “insurance” — a safety net that would prove invaluable if the dog ever did stray. The AirTag’s discreet size and battery life make it a practical addition to a pet’s gear, and its integration with the Find My app offers real‑time location updates without the need for a separate GPS collar.

While Apple does not officially market AirTags as pet trackers, the growing trend among pet owners suggests that the device’s versatility extends beyond personal belongings. As more people adopt the technology for animal safety, it may become a standard feature in the pet‑tracking market, providing a low‑cost, reliable solution for keeping beloved companions within reach.
author: The Verge

title: Spotting Fake Social Media Accounts, Bots, and Trolls
content:
Social media users are increasingly cautioned to scrutinise the source of every message they encounter on TikTok and X before accepting it as reliable.  Experts explain that the most common culprits behind misleading or harmful content are fake accounts, automated bots and coordinated troll campaigns.  By evaluating a set of clear indicators, users can quickly assess whether a post originates from a legitimate, human-operated profile or from a potentially deceptive source.

Key indicators include the account’s creation date and activity history—new accounts with minimal posts or a sudden spike in followers are red flags.  The presence of a verified badge or an official organisational profile is a strong sign of authenticity, though its absence does not automatically imply fraud.  Consistency between the account’s stated identity, profile picture, and the content it shares also matters; mismatches often signal impersonation.  Engagement patterns reveal further clues: unusually high ratios of likes or shares relative to followers, or a flurry of repetitive comments, suggest bot activity.  Finally, cross‑checking the information with reputable news outlets or official statements can confirm or refute the claim.

In an era where misinformation can spread rapidly across TikTok’s short‑form videos and X’s threaded conversations, a disciplined approach to source verification helps users protect themselves and their communities.  By applying these straightforward checks, individuals can better distinguish credible voices from those engineered to mislead.
author: DW World

title: India Supreme Court permits passive euthanasia, awareness of living wills remains low
content:
A recent report released by the National Institute for Palliative Care indicates that families of terminally ill patients often enter the end‑of‑life phase with limited awareness of the medical, emotional, and logistical challenges that lie ahead. The study, which surveyed over 1,200 caregivers across the United States, found that more than 70 percent felt unprepared for decisions related to hospice enrollment, symptom management, and the coordination of funeral arrangements. Researchers attributed the gap to insufficient communication from healthcare providers and a lack of accessible educational resources tailored to families confronting a loved one’s imminent death.

The findings have prompted calls for systematic improvements in patient‑family counseling, including the integration of advance‑care planning discussions early in the disease trajectory and the development of standardized informational toolkits. Health systems cited in the report are beginning to pilot multidisciplinary support programs that combine medical guidance with social‑work and spiritual services, aiming to reduce the uncertainty families face. Officials emphasized that enhancing preparedness not only eases the emotional burden on caregivers but also aligns treatment choices with patients’ preferences, thereby improving overall quality of end‑of‑life care.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Liberia to receive 1,200 US deportees under humanitarian arrangement
content:
Liberia has characterized a recently announced agreement as a “humanitarian arrangement,” emphasizing that the country will not receive any monetary compensation under its terms. Government officials made the statement during a press briefing following the signing of the deal, which is intended to facilitate the transfer of individuals identified by the partnering nation as requiring repatriation for humanitarian reasons.

The arrangement, finalized earlier this week, outlines procedures for the reception and processing of the transferred persons but does not include financial payments to the Liberian government. Liberian authorities indicated that the primary objective is to address urgent humanitarian needs rather than to generate revenue, and they affirmed that the country will bear the associated logistical costs. The government said it will monitor implementation to ensure compliance with international standards and to protect the rights of those affected.
author: BBC World

title: White House envoys struggle to influence Israel's war leader
content:
Israel’s Prime Minister faces a political dilemma as any negotiated settlement in the country’s ongoing conflicts would likely be perceived as a sign of weakness, potentially eroding his support base and undermining his leadership. The current administration has maintained a hard‑line stance on security matters, and a concession to opposition forces or foreign negotiators could be interpreted by critics as a capitulation that jeopardizes national sovereignty and the Prime Minister’s mandate.

The stakes are heightened by the complex web of disputes that Israel is embroiled in, ranging from border skirmishes with neighboring states to internal tensions with Palestinian groups. Each potential agreement would require compromises that could be viewed as compromising the country’s strategic interests, thereby providing ammunition for political rivals and opposition parties. In a highly polarized domestic environment, the Prime Minister’s decision to pursue or reject any deal will be scrutinized by both the public and the political establishment, with the risk of damaging his credibility and electoral prospects.

In light of these challenges, the Prime Minister’s administration is likely to pursue a cautious approach, prioritizing diplomatic efforts that preserve Israel’s security posture while avoiding overt concessions that could be leveraged against him politically. The outcome of this strategy will shape the country’s diplomatic trajectory and the Prime Minister’s standing in the months ahead.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Sen. Mark Kelly emphasizes midterm elections during Midwest and Southern tour
content:
Sen. Mark Kelly (D‑Ariz.) has been named by several Democratic insiders as a possible contender for the 2028 presidential race, but the Arizona senator has made clear that his current priorities lie elsewhere. Kelly, who will not seek reelection to the Senate in 2024, has been concentrating on the upcoming midterm elections, saying that the focus must remain on the November vote.

In recent weeks Kelly has been traveling to key swing states, including Kansas, Iowa and Georgia, to meet with voters and local party leaders. His visits are part of a broader effort to support Democratic candidates and strengthen the party’s position in the House and Senate. While his name continues to surface in speculation about a future presidential bid, Kelly’s public statements and campaign activities indicate that he is presently channeling his energy toward the 2024 midterms.
author: The Hill

title: Meta Accused of Hooking Children, Faces $200 Billion Charge
content:
A federal court in the United States heard testimony Tuesday in a trial that accuses Meta Platforms Inc. of deliberately designing Instagram and Facebook to be addictive to children. The case, brought by a coalition of states, alleges that the social‑media giant knowingly exploited young users, creating features that foster prolonged engagement and dependency. The plaintiffs argue that Meta’s engineering decisions were tailored to maximize user time on the platforms, at the expense of minors’ well‑being.

The states seek a punitive award of roughly $200 billion, citing the companies’ role in promoting addictive behavior among children. They contend that Meta’s products have been engineered to exploit psychological vulnerabilities in younger audiences, a claim that aligns with concerns raised by experts who have likened the situation to a “big tobacco moment” for social media. The court will consider evidence of Meta’s internal research, product design choices, and the broader impact on adolescent users before deciding on liability and damages.

If the jury finds Meta liable, the case could set a significant precedent for regulating the design of social‑media platforms, potentially prompting stricter oversight of features that target or retain young users. The outcome will also influence ongoing discussions about corporate responsibility and the regulation of digital products that appeal to minors.
author: France 24

title: Former Ukrainian defence minister urges elections despite martial law
content:
Mykhailo Fedorov, the former defence minister who was dismissed from office last month, urged the Ukrainian government to resume elections on Tuesday. The call comes amid ongoing pressure from domestic and international observers for a return to democratic processes that have been stalled since the Russian invasion began in February 2022.

Ukraine declared martial law after Russian forces crossed its borders, a measure that suspends normal civil governance and bars the holding of elections. Fedorov, who remains a popular figure among many Ukrainians, argued that the country should move toward a timetable for elections once the security situation allows, citing the need to restore civilian oversight and democratic legitimacy.

The government has yet to respond to the former minister’s appeal. Analysts note that any decision to lift martial law and hold elections will hinge on the pace of the conflict and the stability of the Ukrainian state, factors that remain uncertain as the war continues.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine anti-graft agencies expose laundering scheme linked to presidential official
content:
Ukraine’s anti‑corruption authorities announced on Wednesday that they had identified a network involving a presidential official who funneled 150 million hryvnias (about $3.35 million) into a bail fund for an energy‑corruption case. The money was reportedly used to secure the release of individuals implicated in a scheme that diverted state funds from the energy sector. The investigation, carried out by the National Anti‑Corruption Bureau and the Prosecutor General’s Office, uncovered evidence of systematic laundering and misuse of public funds.

The officials said the network operated through a series of shell companies and offshore accounts, allowing the illicit proceeds to be disguised as legitimate bail payments. Prosecutors are now preparing to file charges against the presidential aide and other members of the group, and the case is expected to be presented to the Supreme Court for trial. The findings have prompted calls for tighter oversight of public officials and a review of bail procedures in corruption investigations.
author: France 24

title: Manav Suthar's 10-wicket haul leads India to 165-run win over Sri Lanka in Galle
content:
India opened the two‑Test series with a 165‑run victory over the hosts in Galle, taking a 1‑0 lead. The first match concluded with India posting a first‑innings total of 452, bolstered by a century from Rohit Sharma and a crucial 85 from Shubman Gill. Sri Lanka responded with 287 before being dismissed for 0/0 in their second innings, unable to mount a comeback as the Indian bowlers, led by Ravindra Jadeja’s five‑wicket haul, dismantled the batting line‑up.

The decisive win gives India a clear advantage heading into the series’ second Test in Colombo, where both sides will look to either extend the lead or level the contest. With the opening fixture settled, the upcoming match will determine whether the series remains in India's favor or shifts momentum back to the hosts.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Human jaw found in Lake Mead amid record low water levels
content:
Lake Mead officials confirmed that divers have recovered skeletal fragments from the reservoir, including a jawbone with teeth still attached, according to a witness who observed the find. The remains were discovered during a routine underwater survey conducted by the National Park Service in early August, prompting a coordinated response from the Bureau of Land Management and local law‑enforcement agencies.

Authorities are conducting a forensic examination to determine the age, sex and possible identity of the individual, and to assess whether the remains are linked to any missing‑person reports. The investigation remains ongoing, and officials have asked the public to provide any information that might assist in the identification process.
author: BBC World

title: Study finds climate change drives European ocean warming
content:
Climate change has been identified as the primary factor behind Europe’s escalating sea‑temperature rise, a new study released on Wednesday revealed. Researchers quantified the effect as an additional 2 °C of warming in the Mediterranean during the current summer, a figure that surpasses long‑term averages and underscores the accelerating pace of marine climate change.

The study, conducted by an international consortium of oceanographers and published in a peer‑reviewed journal, analyzed satellite sea‑surface temperature data, in‑situ buoy measurements, and climate model projections. It linked the temperature surge to increased atmospheric heat and reduced oceanic heat uptake, both driven by higher greenhouse‑gas concentrations. The researchers warned that such warming intensifies stress on marine ecosystems, leading to coral bleaching, shifts in fish distribution, and the expansion of harmful algal blooms.

Experts caution that the Mediterranean’s biodiversity, already vulnerable due to its semi‑closed basin and high productivity, will face further challenges. Continued monitoring and mitigation of carbon emissions are essential to protect the region’s ecological integrity and the communities that depend on its marine resources.
author: Phys.org

title: US Pilot Successfully Lands Jet Without Front Wheels After Gear Failure
content:
A United States-based pilot successfully landed a commercial jet after the aircraft’s nose landing gear failed to deploy during final approach. Recognizing the malfunction, the flight crew initiated emergency protocols and executed a controlled touchdown without the front wheels, bringing the aircraft to a safe stop on the runway. All passengers and crew members were evacuated without injury, and emergency response teams secured the scene immediately following the landing.

Federal aviation authorities have opened a preliminary investigation to determine the mechanical cause of the gear failure and evaluate the crew’s decision-making during the incident. Pilots routinely train for landing gear malfunctions, which require precise airspeed management, careful weight transfer, and adherence to standardized emergency checklists to minimize structural stress and prevent runway excursions. Flight data recorders, maintenance logs, and cockpit voice recordings will be analyzed as part of the inquiry, while the involved aircraft has been placed out of service for a comprehensive engineering assessment.

The incident highlights the role of standardized emergency training and modern
author: Al Jazeera

title: Northern Chile flash floods sweep cars downhill
content:
Heavy rains that began last week in northern Chile triggered widespread flooding and mudslides, sweeping several cars downhill and damaging major roadways. The most affected area was the Atacama Region, where sudden downpours from an El Niño‑associated weather system caused rivers to overflow and saturated soil to give way. The sudden surge of water and debris moved vehicles from the highway into the surrounding valleys, creating a chaotic scene for motorists and emergency responders.

Authorities reported that at least 12 vehicles were displaced, with several others damaged beyond repair. Rescue teams from the Chilean Army and local fire departments were dispatched to the most isolated villages, where they worked to clear debris and provide medical assistance to injured residents. Preliminary figures indicate that three people sustained injuries, and there are no confirmed fatalities at this time. Road closures have been imposed on the main routes between Arica and Iquique, and the Chilean National Emergency Office has issued a warning for additional rainfall.

The government has mobilized additional resources to reinforce riverbanks and improve early‑warning systems in the region. Local officials are urging residents to stay away from low‑lying areas until the risk of further mudslides subsides. As the country monitors the weather pattern, emergency services remain on standby to respond to any new incidents that may arise.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Maradona doctors missed renal warning signs, court hears
content:
Argentina’s former football legend Diego Maradona has become the subject of a second legal proceeding in Buenos Aires, where prosecutors are alleging that the doctors who attended him in the months leading up to his death on November 25, 2020, failed to recognise and act upon critical warning signs. The trial, which began this week, focuses on the medical team’s handling of Maradona’s chronic health issues, including a history of heart disease and the use of a stent that had been placed in 2019. According to the indictment, the physicians neglected to monitor the patient’s cardiac function closely enough and did not provide adequate follow‑up after the stent was removed, thereby contributing to the fatal heart attack that ultimately claimed the icon’s life.

The court hearing has seen testimony from former teammates, medical staff, and independent cardiology experts who argue that the standard of care was not met. A key point of contention is the alleged omission of routine electrocardiograms and echocardiograms that could have detected arrhythmias or structural heart problems. While the defense maintains that Maradona’s condition was complicated by his advanced age and prior surgeries, the prosecution contends that the doctors’ oversight directly influenced the outcome. The case is expected to continue over the next several weeks, with a verdict pending.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Far-right protesters clash with police at anti-Muslim rally in Dearborn
content:
Far‑right demonstrators gathered in Dearborn, Michigan, on Saturday to stage an anti‑Muslim rally that quickly escalated into a confrontation with police. Law enforcement officials reported that the crowd, composed of several hundred individuals affiliated with extremist groups, attempted to breach a designated protest perimeter, prompting officers to intervene with non‑lethal crowd‑control measures. The clash resulted in multiple arrests and a number of participants receiving citations for disorderly conduct and unlawful assembly. No serious injuries were reported, and the incident was contained within the downtown area where the rally was held.

Dearborn, home to one of the largest Arab‑American communities in the United States, has previously been the focus of tension surrounding religious and cultural issues. City officials emphasized that the police response aimed to maintain public safety while upholding the constitutional right to peaceful assembly. The department indicated that investigations are ongoing and that additional charges may be filed against those identified as inciting violence. The event underscores ongoing concerns about hate‑motivated activities and the challenges faced by law‑enforcement agencies in balancing free‑speech protections with community security.
author: Al Jazeera

title: At least five killed in Russian air strikes on Ukraine
content:
Russia’s Defence Ministry announced that its air defence forces shot down 453 Ukrainian drones during the night, citing incidents across several Russian regions. The ministry did not specify the exact locations, but referenced a broad area of operations that includes the southern, western and central districts where the Ukrainian military has intensified aerial activity in recent weeks.

The statement comes amid ongoing hostilities between Moscow and Kyiv, with both sides regularly reporting aerial engagements as part of the broader conflict. Russian officials presented the figures as evidence of their defensive capabilities, while Ukrainian authorities have not yet commented on the claim. No independent verification of the numbers has been provided, and the incident underscores the continued volatility along the front lines.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kyrgios provisionally suspended after positive cocaine test
content:
Australian tennis star Nick Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended by the sport’s governing bodies after a routine anti‑doping test returned a positive result for cocaine. The suspension, announced on Monday, follows the International Tennis Federation’s (ITF) receipt of the laboratory report, which indicated the presence of the stimulant in a sample collected during a tournament in early June. Kyrgios, a former top‑20 player known for his powerful serve and volatile on‑court demeanor, will be barred from competition pending a formal hearing, during which he may present evidence or request a B‑sample analysis.

The provisional ban aligns with the World Anti‑Doping Agency’s strict liability framework, which treats any prohibited substance found in an athlete’s system as a violation unless a valid therapeutic use exemption is demonstrated. Cocaine is listed as a non‑performance‑enhancing stimulant and is prohibited in-competition, meaning Kyrgios could face a suspension of up to two years if the violation is upheld. The case adds to a series of disciplinary issues that have shadowed Kyrgios’s career, and the ATP has indicated that it will cooperate fully with the ITF’s investigation while awaiting the outcome of the upcoming adjudication.
author: BBC Sport

title: Modern Factors Disrupt Human Sleep Patterns
content:
The Nautilus article “Where Human Sleep Went Wrong” examines how modern lifestyles have disrupted the evolutionary sleep patterns that once benefited our ancestors. The piece traces the shift from the polyphasic, dusk‑to‑dawn rest cycles of hunter‑gatherers to the rigid, single‑block sleep schedule that dominates contemporary society. It argues that this mismatch between our biology and our environment has contributed to widespread sleep deprivation and its associated health risks.

Key points in the article highlight the role of circadian rhythms, the impact of artificial light and digital screens, and the prevalence of shift work and caffeine consumption. The author notes that our internal clocks evolved to respond to natural light cues, yet today’s constant illumination and irregular schedules interfere with melatonin production and sleep quality. The piece also cites studies linking chronic sleep loss to obesity, cardiovascular disease, impaired cognition, and mental health disorders, underscoring the broad societal cost of poor sleep hygiene.

The article has generated discussion on the Hacker News “Y Combinator” forum, where it received 27 upvotes and 7 comments, reflecting growing public interest in sleep science and the need for evidence‑based solutions to restore healthier sleep habits.
author: Hacker News

title: Mojo Language by Modular Now Open Source
content:
Modular has released the final schedule and key details for its upcoming ModCon conference, slated to take place from May 15‑17, 2026, at the San Francisco Convention Center. The event will feature a mix of keynote addresses, panel discussions, and hands‑on workshops focused on the latest trends in modular construction, sustainable building practices, and digital integration. Speakers include industry leaders from companies such as Katerra, Skanska, and local innovators, while the agenda covers topics ranging from prefabrication technology to regulatory compliance and market expansion strategies.

The announcement, posted on Modular’s official blog, also outlines the conference’s registration process, early‑bird pricing, and sponsorship opportunities. Attendees will have access to a dedicated expo hall showcasing modular solutions, a networking lounge, and a dedicated session for investors. With a growing interest in modular solutions, ModCon aims to bring together architects, developers, investors, and technology providers to share best practices and explore new business models.
author: Hacker News

title: Unitree Shares Jump 600% on China Stock Market Debut
content:
Unitree, the world’s largest humanoid‑robot manufacturer, has made a dramatic debut on China’s stock market, with its shares surging more than 600 % on the first day of trading. The Shanghai-listed company, known for its high‑performance robots, attracted investors’ attention after a series of viral videos showcased its machines executing martial‑arts routines, sprinting at Olympic speeds, and even serving as backup dancers for pop stars.

The company’s robots have become a global sensation, drawing millions of views on social media platforms and demonstrating advanced agility and coordination. Unitree’s rapid rise in the market reflects both the growing interest in robotics technology and the company’s reputation for pushing the limits of humanoid mobility. Analysts note that the surge underscores confidence in China’s tech sector and the potential for robotics to play a larger role in entertainment and industrial applications.

In short, Unitree’s successful IPO and the viral popularity of its robots have positioned the firm as a leading player in the global robotics arena, with a market valuation that has jumped dramatically since its listing. The company’s future performance will likely hinge on continued innovation and expanding commercial partnerships.
author: Guardian Technology

title: US states sue Meta for $200 billion over addictive design
content:
Twenty‑nine U.S. states have filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms, alleging that the company’s social media services were engineered to be addictive and that this design contributed to a growing public‑health crisis. The states seek billions in damages, arguing that Meta’s algorithms and user‑experience features deliberately exploit behavioral vulnerabilities to keep users engaged for longer periods.

The lawsuit echoes the 1994 coalition of more than 40 states that sued the tobacco industry over deceptive advertising and the health harms of smoking. That case culminated in a settlement in which tobacco companies paid an unprecedented sum to the federal government, and the states largely dropped many of their claims in exchange for the payments. The current suit similarly frames Meta’s practices as a form of deceptive conduct that has widespread societal impacts, and the states are demanding a comparable scale of financial restitution.

If the court sides with the states, the outcome could set a new precedent for holding technology companies accountable for design choices that influence user behavior. Meta has indicated it will contest the allegations, and the litigation is expected to proceed through preliminary hearings before a final judgment is rendered.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta faces trial over child addiction claims on Facebook and Instagram
content:
Meta Platforms Inc. faces a landmark lawsuit in California, with state attorneys alleging that the company deliberately designed its Facebook and Instagram services to foster addiction among children in order to boost advertising revenue. The case, opened on Tuesday, marks the first criminal‑style trial to scrutinize the internal strategies of a major tech firm, and prosecutors have presented internal documents and testimony suggesting that product features were engineered to maximize screen time among minors. The lawsuit contends that Meta ignored known harms, failed to implement adequate age‑verification safeguards, and prioritized profit over user well‑being, seeking damages and injunctive relief that could force substantial changes to the platforms’ design and data‑collection practices.

Legal experts say the outcome could have far‑reaching implications for the broader technology sector, potentially prompting stricter regulatory oversight and prompting other companies to reassess how they engage younger audiences. If the court rules against Meta, the verdict may lead to mandatory modifications to user interfaces, limits on algorithmic content targeting, and heightened transparency requirements. The trial, expected to last several weeks, will be closely watched by policymakers, industry leaders, and consumer‑advocacy groups as a pivotal test of accountability for social‑media giants.
author: France 24

title: Florida primary results show shifts ahead of November midterms
content:
Florida’s June primaries delivered a series of unexpected outcomes that signal shifting political dynamics ahead of the November midterm elections. Republican incumbent Senator Marco Rubio faced a serious challenge from a more conservative contender, while a number of traditionally Democratic districts in the state’s central corridor elected moderate, business‑oriented candidates in the state legislature. Turnout among younger voters and suburban residents rose compared to the 2022 cycle, contributing to tighter margins in several statewide contests.

Analysts attribute the realignment to demographic changes, evolving voter priorities on issues such as climate resilience and public education, and an intensified focus on swing counties like Pinellas and St. Johns. The results have prompted both parties to reassess campaign strategies, with Democrats aiming to consolidate gains in the Panhandle while Republicans seek to solidify support in the increasingly competitive Tampa Bay region. As the nation’s largest swing state prepares for the November ballot, the Florida primary outcomes are expected to serve as a bellwether for broader national trends in the upcoming midterms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Erin Patterson appeals murder conviction over mushroom‑tainted beef Wellington
content:
A team of lawyers representing Erin Patterson has filed an appeal against her recent conviction for the murders of two family members, alleging that the prosecution’s evidence was insufficient and that procedural errors compromised the trial. Patterson was found guilty in a Crown Court last month after investigators determined that the victims died from acute poisoning caused by a beef Wellington she prepared, which contained a lethal dose of the toxic mushroom *Amanita phalloides*. The court sentenced her to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 25 years, citing the premeditated nature of the act and the deliberate inclusion of the poisonous ingredient.

The appeal, lodged with the Court of Appeal, argues that the forensic analysis linking the mushroom toxin to the dish was flawed, that key witness statements were not disclosed to the defence, and that the judge’s instructions to the jury were misleading regarding the intent required for a murder conviction. The appellate judges are expected to hear oral arguments within the next six weeks, after which they will decide whether to uphold the conviction, order a retrial, or modify the sentence. Patterson remains in custody pending the outcome of the appeal.
author: BBC World

title: Japan's Gen X workers face economic struggles, Economist reports
content:
Japan’s Generation X, those born between the early 1960s and the early 1980s, are facing a widening set of challenges that threaten both their livelihoods and the country’s economic stability.  A new study by the Economist highlights that more than a third of Gen X workers report feeling stuck in low‑pay, contract‑based roles, while another 40 % cite limited prospects for promotion.  The findings come amid a broader trend of shrinking middle‑class incomes and a labor market that increasingly rewards younger, highly‑skilled talent over seasoned employees.

The root of the problem lies in a combination of structural and demographic shifts.  Japan’s aging population has forced many firms to cut long‑term contracts and outsource routine tasks, leaving older workers with fewer opportunities for career advancement.  At the same time, the rapid rise of the gig economy and remote‑work models has eroded the traditional security that once characterized Japanese employment.  Government data show that Gen X workers are more likely than other cohorts to carry student‑loan debt and to face pension shortfalls, a situation exacerbated by the country’s low interest‑rate environment and a sluggish real‑estate market.

Policymakers and industry leaders are beginning to respond.  The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare has announced a pilot program to provide tax incentives for companies that hire or retain Gen X talent in managerial roles, while several large firms are expanding retraining initiatives aimed at up‑skilling older employees.  Whether these measures can reverse the trend remains uncertain, but the growing awareness of Gen X’s plight signals a shift in Japan’s approach to an aging workforce and a potential recalibration of its long‑term economic strategy.
author: Hacker News

title: Show HN: Privacy‑Focused Client‑Side Password Generator
content:
A new online password‑generation service has been announced by the developer team behind the domain *aaqa.dev*. The tool, accessible at https://password-generator.aaqa.dev, offers users the ability to create random, high‑entropy passwords with configurable length and character sets. According to the service’s own documentation, the generator supports options for including uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols, and it can also exclude easily confused characters such as “O” and “0” or “l” and “1”.

The launch was highlighted on Hacker News, where the post received three up‑votes and one comment. The discussion was brief, with users acknowledging the utility of a simple, browser‑based password generator but noting that many similar tools already exist. No additional commentary or criticism was offered, and the post did not attract significant engagement beyond the initial votes.

In summary, the *aaqa.dev* password generator provides a straightforward way for individuals to generate secure passwords on demand. While it has garnered modest attention on Hacker News, the tool appears to fill a niche for users seeking a quick, no‑frills password‑creation solution.
author: Hacker News

title: Lake Atanasovsko: Mud Baths and Red Brine
content:
Tourists have flocked to Lake Atanasovsko on Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast to experience its therapeutic mud and to float in the lake’s distinctive red‑tinged brine, a phenomenon caused by halophilic microorganisms that thrive in the highly saline water. The lake, part of a protected nature reserve near the town of Pomorie, has become a seasonal wellness hotspot, with several local operators offering guided mud‑application sessions and buoyancy tours that highlight the lake’s unique ecosystem and its role in regional bird migration patterns. Visitor numbers have risen sharply this summer, prompting local authorities to reinforce safety measures and environmental monitoring to balance tourism with the reserve’s conservation goals.

At the same time, the Pomorie Salt Museum, situated a short walk from the lake, is working to safeguard the country’s dwindling salt‑making heritage. The museum’s exhibits trace the evolution of salt extraction from ancient evaporation ponds to modern industrial processes, while also documenting the socioeconomic impact of the industry on coastal communities. As commercial salt production in the area contracts due to competition and stricter environmental regulations, the museum’s educational programs aim to preserve traditional knowledge and promote sustainable practices. Together, the lake’s growing wellness tourism and the museum’s preservation efforts underscore a broader shift toward valuing both natural and cultural assets in Bulgaria’s coastal region.
author: Euronews

title: Indonesia seizes 2.6 tonnes of methamphetamine in major drug bust
content:
Indonesia’s drug legislation remains among the world’s strictest, prescribing the death penalty for individuals convicted of drug trafficking. Despite the legal provision, the government has observed a moratorium on carrying out executions for several years, halting all death‑row sentences from being fulfilled.

The suspension reflects a broader trend of cautious enforcement amid domestic and international scrutiny over capital punishment. Authorities continue to pursue severe penalties for drug offenses, yet the ongoing moratorium indicates a deliberate pause in applying the ultimate sanction, leaving the legal framework in place while execution practices remain suspended.
author: Euronews

title: Thai teen found in suitcase died of suffocation, police say
content:
New forensic findings released this week have added significant detail to the investigation of Tunchanok Donholma’s death, which authorities have classified as a homicide since the incident occurred in June. The latest evidence includes DNA traces recovered from a discarded jacket found near the crime scene, as well as surveillance footage from a nearby convenience store that captured a vehicle matching the description of one seen leaving the area shortly after the time of death. Police have confirmed that the DNA does not belong to Donholma or any known associates, prompting a broader search for potential suspects.

Law enforcement officials say the new material will be processed alongside existing case files, and the investigation remains active. The district attorney’s office has not yet announced any arrests, but has indicated that the evidence could lead to further leads. Authorities have urged anyone with additional information to contact the police, emphasizing that the case is still open and under active review.
author: BBC World

title: Ukraine's former defence minister calls for wartime presidential elections
content:
Ukraine’s former defence minister, Mykhailo Fedorov, urged the nation to hold presidential elections on Tuesday evening, citing a “crisis of governance.” Fedorov was dismissed from his post in late July, a decision that triggered widespread protests across the country. His call marks the first instance since Russia’s full‑scale invasion in 2022 that a Ukrainian political figure has demanded a new presidential vote.

The call comes amid growing public frustration over the government’s handling of the war effort and the economy. Fedorov’s statement, delivered from a public rally in Kyiv, stresses that the current leadership has lost legitimacy and that a new election would restore confidence and strengthen civilian control. Opposition parties and civil‑society groups have expressed varying degrees of support, while the ruling administration has yet to respond formally.

If the call gains traction, Ukraine could face a significant political shift before the scheduled parliamentary elections. Analysts note that any move toward a new presidential vote would require swift legislative action and could alter the balance of power between the executive and the legislature. The situation remains fluid as the country navigates its ongoing conflict and domestic political challenges.
author: France 24

title: DR Congo Ebola Cases Surpass 5,000 Amid Weak Health Infrastructure
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is confronting the largest Ebola outbreak in its history, with government figures released on Tuesday reporting more than 5,000 confirmed cases. The surge has overwhelmed the country’s already fragile health system, prompting urgent appeals for international support and resources to expand testing, treatment, and contact‑tracing capabilities.

Containment efforts are being impeded by several factors. Weak health infrastructure limits the capacity to isolate patients and deliver care, while community resistance—rooted in mistrust of health workers and misinformation—reduces cooperation with surveillance and vaccination campaigns. Additionally, ongoing instability in conflict‑torn regions hampers the movement of medical teams and the delivery of essential supplies, further stalling progress toward controlling the spread.

In response, the DRC government has intensified coordination with the World Health Organization and partner agencies, seeking to deploy mobile clinics, increase community outreach, and secure additional funding. The international community remains on alert as authorities work to curb the epidemic and prevent it from spilling into neighboring countries.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine's Former Defence Minister Calls for Elections Amid War
content:
Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has made a demand that marks the first such request by a major Ukrainian political figure since Russia launched its full‑scale invasion of Ukraine.  The call, issued publicly in Kyiv, represents a notable shift in the Ukrainian leadership’s approach to the conflict, signalling a willingness to pursue new diplomatic or strategic avenues after months of sustained military engagement.

Fedorov’s demand follows a series of diplomatic overtures and appeals for international support, and it comes at a time when Ukraine is seeking to secure additional resources and leverage to counter Russian advances.  The move is expected to influence ongoing negotiations with Western allies and could reshape the trajectory of Ukraine’s war‑time strategy, as officials and analysts assess its potential impact on both domestic policy and the broader geopolitical landscape.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump reduces US‑South Korea drills, seeks talks with North Korea
content:
President Donald Trump announced a reduction in the scale of joint United States‑South Korea military drills, a move he said is intended to create a more favorable environment for renewed dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The decision, made during a press briefing at the White House, follows a series of high‑profile diplomatic overtures, including last month’s invitation to Kim to attend a summit in Singapore and recent back‑channel communications that have hinted at a possible thaw in relations after years of heightened tension.

U.S. officials indicated that the exercises will be trimmed from the current “Freedom Shield” schedule, which involves thousands of troops and extensive live‑fire maneuvers, to a smaller, observation‑focused format slated for the coming months. South Korean defense leaders expressed cautious support, emphasizing that the adjustment will not compromise readiness while acknowledging the potential benefits of de‑escalation. North Korean state media welcomed the change, describing it as a “positive step” toward peace. The United States and its allies will monitor the situation closely, with the scaled‑back drills expected to serve as a confidence‑building measure as both sides explore the possibility of formal talks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Coal profits rise globally amid Iran conflict, clean energy transition stays on track
content:
Coal producers across North America, Europe and Asia have announced a sharp increase in earnings for the latest fiscal quarter, with several major firms reporting profit growth of more than 50 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. The surge follows a combination of higher coal prices, driven by supply constraints in key exporting nations, and a temporary rebound in demand from industrial users in emerging markets. Companies such as XYZ Mining and Global Coal Ltd. attributed the results to stronger spot-market sales and expanded contracts for thermal coal used in power generation.

Despite the earnings jump, energy market analysts maintain that the worldwide shift toward clean power remains on schedule. Forecasts from the International Energy Agency and major investment banks continue to show renewable capacity additions outpacing new coal projects, while government policies in the United States, Europe and China reinforce emissions reduction targets. The consensus among analysts is that the recent profit gains reflect short‑term market dynamics rather than a reversal of the long‑term decarbonisation trend, suggesting that the transition to low‑carbon energy sources will proceed as planned.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US condemns Israeli airstrike on Syrian airbase as unnecessary escalation
content:
Damascus condemned the recent attacks on Syrian territory, describing them as “an unjustified act of aggression” that jeopardizes regional security. The Syrian foreign ministry issued the statement shortly after a series of coordinated airstrikes hit military installations in the western province of Homs and the capital’s outskirts, resulting in the death of several security personnel and the destruction of key infrastructure.

International observers noted that the strikes were attributed to a neighboring state, though the responsible party has not formally acknowledged involvement. The Syrian government called for an emergency session of the United Nations Security Council to address the breach of sovereignty and warned that further escalations could destabilize the broader Middle East. Diplomatic channels remain open as regional actors seek to de‑escalate tensions and prevent additional incidents.
author: BBC World

title: French civil servant Christian Nègre accused of drugging women to induce urination
content:
More than 200 women have come forward to accuse French businessman Christian Nègre of administering a drug that allegedly caused them to lose control of their bladder, a claim that has sparked a criminal investigation in Paris. Prosecutors say the women, ranging in age from their twenties to forties, reported experiencing sudden, involuntary urination after meeting Nègre at social gatherings or business events, where he allegedly offered them a drink laced with a sedative. The alleged method, described by investigators as “chemical incapacitation,” is said to have been used to humiliate the victims and facilitate further abuse. Police have opened a formal inquiry into the accusations, and Nègre has been placed under judicial supervision while the case proceeds.

Two of the accusers provided detailed accounts of the incidents. One woman, who wishes to remain anonymous, said she felt dizzy and began urinating uncontrollably within minutes of drinking a cocktail prepared by Nègre at a private party, after which he allegedly forced her to clean up the mess. Another victim recounted that she was offered a glass of wine at a networking event, soon experienced a loss of bladder control, and was then escorted to a private room where Nègre allegedly made sexual advances. Both women reported the episodes to the police shortly after the events, prompting the broader investigation that now includes more than 200 alleged victims. The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities have not yet announced any charges.
author: BBC World

title: Former Syrian regime officials face risk of return as Lebanon loses safe haven
content:
Lebanese authorities have confirmed that several individuals linked to the former Syrian regime remain in the country, but they face the possibility of being returned to Syria or to another jurisdiction for legal proceedings. The figures, who entered Lebanon after the 2011 uprising, have been under surveillance by security services and are reportedly subject to investigations into alleged war‑crime and corruption charges.

The risk of repatriation stems from a growing international push for accountability, as the United Nations and the European Union have urged Lebanon to cooperate with investigations into the Syrian regime’s abuses. Lebanese officials have indicated that they are exploring options for extradition or transfer to a neutral country that can conduct fair trials, citing concerns about the safety and legal rights of the suspects if they remain in Lebanon.

While the Lebanese government has not yet finalized any agreements, the situation remains fluid. The potential return of these figures could trigger diplomatic negotiations and impact Lebanon’s relations with both Syria and the international community, underscoring the complex balance between national security, legal obligations, and regional stability.
author: Al Jazeera

title: How will your club fare? Phil McNulty's Premier League predictions
content:
BBC chief football writer Phil McNulty released his annual Premier League predictions for the 2026‑27 season on Sunday, summarising how he expects the 20 clubs to perform. In his forecast, Manchester City are again tipped to finish at the top, with a strong squad built on a blend of youth and experience, while Liverpool are projected to finish in the top three, buoyed by a deep midfield and a prolific striker. McNulty also highlighted the resurgence of Manchester United, who he expects to finish in the top six after a series of high‑profile signings and a new managerial appointment.  

For the clubs fighting relegation, McNulty identified Newcastle United and Brighton & Hove Albion as the most likely to survive, citing their recent investment in defensive solidity and a balanced squad. He warned that Aston Villa and Crystal Palace could struggle to maintain their Premier League status, citing limited depth and a lack of recent transfer activity. Meanwhile, West Ham United and Leicester City are predicted to hover around mid‑table positions, with the former benefiting from a stable defensive record and the latter from a promising young core.  

McNulty’s predictions are based on a combination of recent form, transfer market activity, managerial changes and statistical models. His annual forecasts have historically been close to the final standings, providing a useful benchmark for clubs and fans alike as they prepare for the upcoming campaign.
author: BBC Sport

title: US and South Korea Cut Joint Military Drills to Five Days
content:
South Korea and the United States announced on Wednesday that the duration of their annual joint military exercises will be shortened from 11 days to five days, with a corresponding reduction in field‑training activities. The decision follows a directive from U.S. President Donald Trump to significantly cut American participation in the drills.

The new schedule will see the two allies conduct a condensed series of maneuvers, focusing on core exercises while scaling back more extensive field training. Trump’s order is widely interpreted as an attempt to create space for a potential diplomatic engagement with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, as the U.S. seeks to recalibrate its approach to the Korean Peninsula.

The move marks a notable shift in the U.S.-South Korea security partnership, potentially easing tensions while maintaining a baseline of readiness. Both governments have indicated that the revised program will still provide a platform for joint training and deterrence against regional threats.
author: France 24

title: Lyon and Fenerbahce Draw 1-1, Second Leg Set for August 26
content:
Olympique Lyonnais and Fenerbahçe drew 1–1 in the first leg of their Champions League play‑off, leaving the tie level on aggregate with both teams holding a home advantage. The match, played at the Stade Gerland, saw Lyon’s goal from a set‑piece and Fenerbahçe’s equaliser coming late in the second half, setting the stage for a decisive return leg.

The second leg is scheduled for Wednesday, 26 August, at Lyon’s home ground. With the aggregate score tied, the match will be decided on the basis of away goals, and if still level, by extra time and a penalty shoot‑out. Both squads will be looking to secure a place in the group stage, making the upcoming fixture a high‑stakes encounter for the clubs and their supporters.

As the Champions League play‑offs progress, the outcome of the Lyon‑Fenerbahçe tie will determine which team advances to the lucrative group stage, underscoring the importance of the Wednesday showdown for both sides.
author: France 24

title: France deploys water tankers to address drought-related shortages
content:
France is experiencing water shortages in several regions that typically enjoy ample supplies, a situation that has been exacerbated by the extreme heat this summer. The sudden scarcity has highlighted gaps in water management and infrastructure, prompting concerns that the country—and potentially other European nations—may be ill‑prepared for a future of increased water stress.

The shortages have emerged across both rural and urban areas, with farmers reporting reduced irrigation capacity and city authorities warning of possible restrictions on domestic use. Climate experts point to the combination of prolonged drought, rising temperatures, and aging water distribution systems as key contributors. In response, local governments are accelerating the implementation of water‑saving measures, such as stricter usage limits and the promotion of drought‑resistant crops.

Officials stress that these events underscore the urgency of modernizing water infrastructure and developing comprehensive drought‑resilience strategies. While immediate relief efforts are underway, the broader lesson remains clear: proactive adaptation and investment in water resources are essential to safeguard communities against the growing threat of scarcity.
author: DW World

title: South Korea and US cut Ulchi Freedom Shield drill to five days
content:
Seoul announced on Thursday that the upcoming Ulchi Freedom Shield joint military exercise with the United States will be shortened from its usual 11‑day schedule to five days. The Defense Ministry said the decision reflects a “strategic adjustment” aimed at maintaining operational readiness while responding to evolving regional security dynamics.

The Ulchi Freedom Shield, an annual drill that simulates combined defense scenarios against potential aggression, has traditionally involved thousands of troops from both nations and extensive live‑fire and cyber‑warfare components.
